Q0001 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When you're at an intersection, when must you not pass a vehicle on the left?
  • [A] When the other car has stopped
  • [B] When the other car is indicating right
  • [C] When the other car is indicating left ✔ Correct
Explanation: You must not pass on the left if a vehicle is indicating left because there is a risk that it will turn into your path.
Q0002 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Your rear red stop light is not working but you have a current warrant of fitness. What should you do?
  • [A] You are ok to drive like this until your next WoF
  • [B] The vehicle must be fixed immediately ✔ Correct
  • [C] It is ok as long as you only drive during daylight hours
Explanation: A police may pull you over and could fine you if your car is deemed unsafe.
Q0003 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When you come to a one-lane bridge, what should you do?
  • [A] You can continue to cross if you reach the bridge first
  • [B] Flash your lights and slow down to warn oncoming cars if you don't have the right of way
  • [C] Slow down, be prepared to stop and only go ahead if the bridge is clear of oncoming traffic ✔ Correct
  • [D] If you have a blue sign with a white arrow in your direction then you can go
Explanation: Answer C is correct.
Q0004 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Legally who may require you to give a blood sample?
  • [A] An ambulance officer
  • [B] A police officer ✔ Correct
  • [C] A lawyer
  • [D] None of the above
Explanation: A medical doctor or other approved professional will take the blood sample but it is the police officer who can require you to give the sample. You may be arrested if you don't comply and refuse an evidential breath test.
Q0005 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When you are turning right, when must you signal?
  • [A] Signalling is only required if there is traffic behind or in front of you
  • [B] Always, for a minimum of two seconds before you turn
  • [C] Always, for a minimum of three seconds before you turn ✔ Correct
Explanation: A safe time to signal for is three seconds as it allows enough time for other road users to understand your intentions.
Q0006 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What do police officer's directions overrule at a traffic light?
  • [A] Traffic lights
  • [B] Give Way rules
  • [C] Road signs, such as stop signs
  • [D] All of the above ✔ Correct
Explanation: An intersection a police officer's directions overrule all other signs and signals.
Q0007 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When you come to a one-lane bridge, what should you do?
  • [A] You can continue to cross if you reach the bridge first
  • [B] If you don't have the right of way slow down and flash your high beams to notify other drivers
  • [C] Slow down, be prepared to stop and only proceed if the bridge is clear of oncoming traffic ✔ Correct
  • [D] Proceed only if you have a green arrow pointing straight ahead
Explanation: Answer C is correct.
Q0008 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Your vehicle headlights must be turned on when?
  • [A] 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise
  • [B] In fog
  • [C] When you can't see 100 metres ahead of you
  • [D] All of the above ✔ Correct
Explanation: Using your lights will make you more visible, all of these situations mean your vehicle is less visible to other road users. Note that it is mandatory to turn your headlights or daytime running lights on during daylight hours if you are riding a motorbike that was manufactured...
Q0009 All Classes Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When you are towing a trailer at night what must be displayed on the back?
  • [A] A red light ✔ Correct
  • [B] A sign with a blue arrow
  • [C] A yellow light
  • [D] A flashing orange light
Explanation: A red light must be displayed on the back of the trailer.
Q0010 All Classes Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
A trailer is being towed at night, what must be displayed on the back of it?
  • [A] A red light ✔ Correct
  • [B] A yellow light
  • [C] A green light
  • [D] A flashing red light
Explanation: Correct. A red light is mandatory on the back of the trailer.
Q0011 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
The legal definition of a road is what?
  • [A] It does not matter if there are lines painted or not, any sealed or unsealed street or highway is considered a road
  • [B] Any area the public is reasonably allowed to drive on at times, including streets, highways, riverbeds, beaches, wharves and car parks ✔ Correct
  • [C] All streets and highways with painted lines indicating lanes
Explanation: Car parks, beaches, road shoulders, bridges, riverbeds, and wharves are all included in the definition of a road.
Q0012 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
The two-second rule has what purpose? Check any that apply.
  • [A] Overtaking vehicles are able to move back into the line of traffic safely if required
  • [B] To give you enough time to stop if the vehicle in front stops ✔ Correct
  • [C] If required two seconds is enough time to stop in any weather conditions.
Explanation: The two-second rule should be applied to assist you in stopping safely only if it's dry weather. In wet weather, you should apply the four-second rule. As regards overtaking, a vehicle should not overtake if the manoeuvre cannot be completed safely.
Q0013 All Classes Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
How often does your vehicle that was registered on the 1st of January 2000, but is at least 3 years old, require a Warrant of Fitness Inspection?
  • [A] Every month
  • [B] Every 6 months
  • [C] Every 12 months ✔ Correct
  • [D] Every 2 years
Explanation: If the vehicle was first registered on or after 1 January 2000 anywhere in the world then it moves to annual WOFs for the lifetime of the vehicle. After an initial inspection for new vehicles, another WoF inspection won't be required until the third anniversary of their first...
Q0014 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
You must give way to all vehicles coming towards you that are turning right (if you are turning left at an intersection)? True or False.
  • [A] TRUE
  • [B] FALSE ✔ Correct
Explanation: If you are turning left, you have the right of way.
Q0015 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What is a courtesy crossing?
  • [A] It's a pedestrian crossing controlled by yellow flashing lights
  • [B] It's the green man symbol that notifies pedestrians when it is safe to cross at traffic lights
  • [C] It is not a required stop, but if pedestrians want to cross it is a raised crossing in the road that allows for a safe place to stop. ✔ Correct
Explanation: They are not official, but they provide a safe place for drivers to stop and for pedestrians to cross. They are normally made of bricks or paving and are often raised above the level of the road.
Q0016 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When MUST you always dip your headlights on your vehicle at night? Check all that apply.
  • [A] When other vehicles are driving towards you ✔ Correct
  • [B] When you are following other vehicles
  • [C] When traffic is being directed by a police officer
  • [D] When you park your car
  • [E] E. When you are backing out of a driveway
Explanation: Correct. A, B, C, and D are all examples of when you must dip your headlights. You don't need to dip your headlights if there's no danger of you A, B, C or D happening while you are performing a reversing manoeuvre.
Q0017 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What does this marking mean?
  • [A] Electric and hybrid vehicles can be charged here
  • [B] Only buses can park here
  • [C] Cycle lane ahead
  • [D] Fire hydrant ✔ Correct
Explanation: The location of a fire hydrant is marked.
Q0018 All Classes Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Can you carry passengers if you have a learner licence?
  • [A] No
  • [B] Yes
  • [C] Yes, but only if a supervisor agrees to it ✔ Correct
Explanation: If the person supervising agrees to it then you can carry passengers in your car. They will be responsible for the passengers and your actions while driving.
Q0019 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you do if you are turning right at traffic signals showing a red arrow pointing to the right?
  • [A] Stop until it's safe to proceed and you've gotten a green arrow
  • [B] Stop until you get a green traffic light and the red arrow disappears, then proceed with the Give Way rules
  • [C] Both a and b are correct ✔ Correct
Explanation: Both examples are correct.
Q0020 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you do if after a train has passed the red lights continue to flash at a railway level crossing?
  • [A] Wait, check both ways once they've stopped flashing and then cross ✔ Correct
  • [B] Check both ways and if nothing is coming then cross
  • [C] Wait for 10 seconds and then cross
Explanation: There may be another train coming, you should wait.
Q0021 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Before passing another vehicle, how long should you signal for?
  • [A] One second
  • [B] Two seconds
  • [C] Three seconds ✔ Correct
  • [D] You only need to signal if there's a vehicle behind you
Explanation: Three seconds is the ideal signal time as it gives other vehicles behind you enough time to see your intention, and it allows you enough time to ensure the road ahead is safe and clear.
Q0022 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
You are approaching a roundabout and must give way to all the vehicles that will cross your path from your left? True or False?
  • [A] TRUE
  • [B] FALSE ✔ Correct
Explanation: Like in the diagram, you give way to vehicles coming from your right, not your left.
Q0023 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
How should an entrance way into a public car park be treated, for the purpose of applying the Give Way rule?
  • [A] As an intersection ✔ Correct
  • [B] As a driveway
  • [C] The vehicle that is there first has right of way
  • [D] As a one-way street
Explanation: The Give Way rules are as follows: * If you are turning right at an intersection, give way to vehicles proceeding towards you that are turning left. * Give way to all vehicles that aren't turning, if you are turning at an intersection. * In all other situations, give way to all...
Q0024 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
If you are driving in wet or frosty conditions, what rule should you use to judge a safe following distance?
  • [A] Two-second rule
  • [B] Four-second rule ✔ Correct
  • [C] 100 metre rule
Explanation: It can take up to twice as long to stop when it's wet and frosty outside, so you need to follow the four-second rule. This rule also applies anytime that you are towing a trailer.
Q0025 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
You can be required to undergo a breath screen test by who?
  • [A] A police officer ✔ Correct
  • [B] A fire officer
  • [C] A lawyer
  • [D] A nurse
  • [E] E. None of the above
Explanation: A police officer will ask you to blow into either a tube of crystals with a bag on the end or a small electronic device. If your alcohol level is high, you will be asked to take an evidential breath test or have a blood test.
Q0026 All Classes Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
You have a 15 year old (0-14) in your vehicle. Who is responsible for making them use a safety belt or a safety seat in a vehicle?
  • [A] The person in the car who has had their licence the longest
  • [B] The driver ✔ Correct
  • [C] The passenger
  • [D] The oldest person in the car
Explanation: Passengers 15 years and older are responsible for putting their own seatbelts on while the driver is responsible for ensuring all passengers UNDER 15 years of age wear seatbelts.
Q0027 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Before you turn to the right on a straight road, what must you do? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Signal for a minimum of 3 seconds ✔ Correct
  • [B] Give way to vehicles from the left
  • [C] Give way to vehicles coming straight ahead
  • [D] Shift towards the centre line
  • [E] E. Check your mirrors
Explanation: Before you turn to the right you must signal for three seconds after you have checked your mirrors. Then move towards the centre line and give way to vehicles coming towards you.
Q0028 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
If you're driving in the fog, which of your vehicle's lights do you have on?
  • [A] Park lights (side lights)
  • [B] Front and rear fog lights
  • [C] Dipped headlights
  • [D] All of the above ✔ Correct
Explanation: In the fog you can have all your lights on, but keep your headlights dipped and keep your full beam headlights off as they can reflect back at you and reduce visibility. When the fog clears turn your fog lights off to avoid dazzling other drivers.
Q0029 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When you've finished passing another vehicle what is the least distance of clear road you MUST have in front of you?
  • [A] 75 metres
  • [B] 100 metres ✔ Correct
  • [C] 150 metres
  • [D] 225 metres
Explanation: In order to give you enough time to react to unexpected circumstances you must be able to see at least 100 metres in front of you after you've finished passing.
Q0030 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
If your vehicle is not up to warrant of fitness standard, can you be fined if it is on the road?
  • [A] Yes ✔ Correct
  • [B] No
Explanation: Correct. If something appears to not be up to warrant of fitness standard then a police office can inspect your call by pulling you over.
Q0031 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When you are turning to the right:
  • [A] Give three seconds' warning ✔ Correct
  • [B] Give two seconds' warning
  • [C] Only signal if there are cars behind you
Explanation: This gives the cars following you enough time to respond.
Q0032 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
You must give way to all vehicles coming towards you that are turning right (if you are turning left at an intersection). True or False?
  • [A] TRUE
  • [B] FALSE ✔ Correct
Explanation: False. If you are turning left then you have the right of way.
Q0033 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Are you required to carry your licence at all times when driving as the holder of any class of driver licence?
  • [A] No
  • [B] Yes ✔ Correct
  • [C] Only if you're on a restricted licence
Explanation: Regardless of the type of licence you have, you must carry your driver licence at all times when driving.
Q0034 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When are you permitted to pass on the right of another moving vehicle? Check all that apply.
  • [A] When you start passing you can see 100m in front of you
  • [B] You've signalled right for at least 3 seconds ✔ Correct
  • [C] To get past safely you can exceed the speed limit for a short time
  • [D] Once you've finished passing you can see at least 100m ahead of you
Explanation: B and D are the correct answers. Once you've finished passing you need to see 100m ahead, not when you start passing, and you should not exceed the speed limit.
Q0035 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
You're driving straight through a roundabout, don't signal as you approach the roundabout, only signal left as you pass the exit before the one you wish to take? True or False.
  • [A] TRUE ✔ Correct
  • [B] False.
Explanation: True. You must still indicate on a smaller roundabout, but you may not be able to give the full three second indicator.
Q0036 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What is the legal definition of a road?
  • [A] Any street or highway that is sealed or unsealed and has lines painted on them or not
  • [B] Streets, highways, beaches, wharves, car parks, and riverbeds, or any area that the public is reasonably permitted to drive on. ✔ Correct
  • [C] Highways and streets that have painted lines on them to distinguish lanes
Explanation: The word road has quite an extensive definition. Bridges, road shoulders, riverbeds, beaches, wharves and car parks are also included.
Q0037 All Classes Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
The weight of the trailer must not exceed what weight when towing a trailer on a learner's or restricted car licence?
  • [A] 3000kg
  • [B] 3500kg
  • [C] 4000kg
  • [D] 4500kg ✔ Correct
  • [E] E. 7000kg
Explanation: On a Class 1 learners or restricted license the maximum combined weight of a vehicle plus trailer must not exceed 4500kg. Your vehicle plus trailer can be up to 6000kg on a full licence.
Q0038 All Classes Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Do you have to have your learner licence with you when you are driving as a learner?
  • [A] Yes ✔ Correct
  • [B] No
Explanation: Yes, you must always have your licence with you when you drive.
Q0039 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
If you are under 20 years old, how many standard drinks can you have before driving?
  • [A] One
  • [B] Two
  • [C] Three
  • [D] None ✔ Correct
Explanation: You should not drink just before driving if you are under 20 years old, as the legal limit is 0 milligrams per 100 millilitres of blood.
Q0040 All Classes Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
To prevent too much noise and gases from entering the car, which parts of the car must be in good condition? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Doors
  • [B] Exhaust ✔ Correct
  • [C] Silencer
  • [D] Gas
Explanation: To stop the noise and gases from entering the car, the exhaust and silencer should work.
Q0041 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When you are turning to the right:
  • [A] Give three seconds' warning ✔ Correct
  • [B] Give two seconds' warning
  • [C] Only indicate if there are cars behind you
Explanation: Cars following you will have enough time to reach this way.
Q0042 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When you see red flashing lights from an ambulance or fire engine or when you hear a siren, what must you do?
  • [A] If they're driving behind you speed up so you're not slowing them down
  • [B] Stop where you are immediately
  • [C] Slow down and pull over to allow them to pass. Stop if necessary ✔ Correct
  • [D] Slow down and pull your car up on the footpath
Explanation: You must slow down and pull over if they are behind you and you must stop if necessary. If a police car is following you with its lights flashing, then you must stop. A police car will have blue and red lights.
Q0043 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Another vehicle is moving to it's right, when can you pass? Check all that apply.
  • [A] You can see at least 100m ahead of you when you start passing
  • [B] For three seconds you have signalled right ✔ Correct
  • [C] As long as your passing the other vehicle then it is okay to go over the speed limit
  • [D] You can see at least 100m ahead of you when you've finished passing
Explanation: Both B and D are the correct answers. You should not exceed the speed limit and once you've finished passing, you need to see 100m ahead of you, not when you start passing.
Q0044 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
You may pass on the left at an intersection if you can do it safely, and if:
  • [A] the vehicle beside you is going faster than the speed limit
  • [B] the vehicle behind is signalling a left turn
  • [C] you have your parking lights off
  • [D] the vehicle in front is signalling a right turn ✔ Correct
Explanation: You can pass left at an intersection if you are in another lane or in a turning bay or if a vehicle is indicating right and has moved over toward the right of their lane, then you can overtake on the left if it's safe to proceed and your vehicle will fit through the gap.
Q0045 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
You only need to signal left as you pass the exit of the one you wish to take on the roundabout. You don't need to signal as you come up to the roundabout if you are going straight through. True or false?
  • [A] TRUE ✔ Correct
  • [B] FALSE
Explanation: True. You may not be able to give the required three seconds of indication on a smaller roundabout, but you still must indicate.
Q0046 All Classes Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
A load may overhang your car behind the rear axel by what maximum distance?
  • [A] 1m
  • [B] 2m
  • [C] 3m
  • [D] 4m ✔ Correct
Explanation: A load can overhang up to 4m behind the rear axle but it must not drag on the ground. If the load protrudes more than 1m behind the car you must tie a white, red, yellow, or orange fluorescent flag to it.
Q0047 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What do a police officer's rules overrule at an intersection?
  • [A] Traffic lights
  • [B] Give Way rules
  • [C] Stop signs and all other road signs
  • [D] All of the above ✔ Correct
Explanation: At an intersection, a police officer's directions overrule all other signs and signals.
Q0048 All Classes Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What must a towed vehicle have at the back of it when driving at night?
  • [A] A red light ✔ Correct
  • [B] A blue light
  • [C] One or more orange lights
  • [D] A flashing yellow light
Explanation: One red light must be shown on the trailer or towed vehicle when driving at night.
Q0049 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
From the time you see an accident sign to the time you pass a crash site, what is the speed limit?
  • [A] 20kph ✔ Correct
  • [B] 30kph
  • [C] 40kph
  • [D] 50kph
Explanation: Correct. 20kph is safest at an accident site because there might be debris on the road and people working to clear it up; or there may be other obstructions
Q0050 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
If you are under 20 years old, how many standard drinks can you have before driving?
  • [A] One
  • [B] Two
  • [C] Three
  • [D] None ✔ Correct
Explanation: You must not drink before driving if you are under 20 years old as one drink consumed will most certainly put you over. The legal limit is 0 milligrams per 100 millilitres of blood.
Q0051 All Classes Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
The warrant of fitness label for your car should be displayed where?
  • [A] Rear window, driver's side
  • [B] Rear window, passenger side
  • [C] Front window, driver's side ✔ Correct
  • [D] Front window, passenger side
Explanation: The WoF label is best displayed in the top corner so that it doesn't interfere with your driving vision. It must be displayed on the inside of the front window on the driver's side, and be clearly visible from the outside.
Q0052 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
If you are under 20 years old, how many standard drinks can you have before driving?
  • [A] One
  • [B] Two
  • [C] Three
  • [D] None ✔ Correct
Explanation: You must not drink before driving if you are under 20 years old as one drink consumed will most certainly put you over. The legal limit is 0 milligrams per 100 millilitres of blood.
Q0053 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Your vehicle headlights must be turned on when visibility is less than:
  • [A] 55 metres
  • [B] 100 metres ✔ Correct
  • [C] 170 metres
  • [D] 300 metres
Explanation: If you can't see a person 100 metres away, you are required to turn your lights on. 100 metres is a safe distance.
Q0054 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When you are turning to the right:
  • [A] Give three seconds' warning ✔ Correct
  • [B] Give five seconds' warning
  • [C] Only signal if you can see cars behind or ahead of you
Explanation: This provides the cars following you with enough time to react.
Q0055 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
The headlights on your vehicle MUST be dipped at what time? Check all those that apply.
  • [A] When you are behind other vehicles ✔ Correct
  • [B] when a police officer is directing traffic
  • [C] when you park
  • [D] when other vehicles are approaching you
Explanation: All the options are mandatory. There are other examples where you might dip your lights, such as driving in fog or driving when there is enough light.
Q0056 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
In a 50kph zone (excluding an emergency) when should you use your horn?
  • [A] Between midnight and 6am
  • [B] Between 4pm and 6pm
  • [C] Any time you are near a hospital or in a school zone
  • [D] Between 3pm and 6pm
  • [E] E. Between 11pm and 7am ✔ Correct
Explanation: You should only use your horn when in an urban zone (50kph area) between 11pm and 7am.
Q0057 All Classes Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What hours can you drive on your own if you have a restricted licence?
  • [A] 10pm-5am ✔ Correct
  • [B] Dawn to dusk
  • [C] 5am-6pm
  • [D] 5am-9pm
Explanation: You can drive on your own on a restricted licence as long as you have someone with you from 10pm to 5am.
Q0058 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Which vehicle lights should you turn on when driving at night?
  • [A] Position lights (park lights) only
  • [B] Dipped headlights (low beam) ✔ Correct
  • [C] High beam lights
  • [D] Fog lights
Explanation: First you should turn on your dipped headlights which will also turn on your park lights. You can use your high beam headlights and fog lights if the situation arises, and you can leave your position lights on while you are parked and in the vehicle.
Q0059 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you do if you are turning right at traffic signals that are showing a red arrow pointing to the right?
  • [A] Stop until you see a green arrow and then continue to go if it is safe
  • [B] Stop until you get a green traffic light and the red arrow disappears, then apply the Give Way rules and proceed
  • [C] Both a and b are correct ✔ Correct
Explanation: Both scenarios are correct.
Q0060 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When you're driving in fog, which of your vehicle's lights do you have on?
  • [A] Park lights (side lights)
  • [B] Front and rear fog lights
  • [C] Dipped headlights
  • [D] All of the above ✔ Correct
Explanation: Don't use full beam headlights in fog, as it can reflect back at you and reduce your visibility. You can have all your lights on but keep your highlights dimmed and turn your fog lights off when the fog clears to avoid dazzling other drivers.
Q0061 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When you have finished passing another vehicle, what is the least distance of clear road you MUST have in front of you?
  • [A] 50 metres
  • [B] 100 metres ✔ Correct
  • [C] 150 metres
  • [D] 200 metres
Explanation: After you have finished passing you must be able to see at least 100 metres in front of you to give you enough time to react in unexpected situations.
Q0062 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
At what time are you permitted to pass another moving vehicle to its right?
  • [A] When you start passing you can see 100m in front of you
  • [B] You've signalled right for at least 3 seconds ✔ Correct
  • [C] In order to get past, it's safe to exceed the speed limit for a short time
  • [D] When you've finished passing you can see at least 100m in front of you
Explanation: Once you've finished passing you need to see 100m in front of you, not when you begin passing, and you should not exceed the speed limit. Therefore B and D are the right answers.
Q0063 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Before you turn to the right on a straight road, what must you do? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Signal for at least three seconds ✔ Correct
  • [B] Give way to vehicles from the left
  • [C] Give way to vehicles coming straight ahead
  • [D] Move towards the centre line
  • [E] E. Check your mirrors
Explanation: Before you turn to the right you must signal for three seconds after you have checked your mirrors. Then move towards the centre line and give way to vehicles coming towards you.
Q0064 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
A trailer being towed at night must have what displayed on the back of it?
  • [A] A red light ✔ Correct
  • [B] A blue light
  • [C] A white light
  • [D] A flashing red light
Explanation: Correct. A red light is mandatory on the back of the trailer.
Q0065 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you do if the red lights continue to flash at a railway level crossing after the train has passed?
  • [A] Check both ways and wait until they are no longer flashing to cross ✔ Correct
  • [B] If you look both ways and you see nothing coming then cross
  • [C] Wait for 10 seconds and then drive on
Explanation: This means that there may be another train coming, you should wait.
Q0066 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When you've finished passing another vehicle, what is the least distance of clear road you MUST have in front of you?
  • [A] 75 metres
  • [B] 100 metres ✔ Correct
  • [C] 150 metres
  • [D] 225 metres
Explanation: In order to give you enough time to react to unexpected circumstances you must be able to see at least 100 metres in front of you after you've finished passing.
Q0067 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
You are allowed to pass a vehicle to your left at what point? Check all that apply.
  • [A] You have been directed to by a police officer ✔ Correct
  • [B] It's safe to pass and there are two or more lanes on your side of the road
  • [C] The car you will pass is either slowing down or has stopped and is signalling a right turn
  • [D] There isn't enough room to pass safely on a single lane road as the vehicle is either a motorcycle or scooter
Explanation: The correct answers are A, B and C. When you pass motorbikes and scooters, you must maintain a safe distance as they can easily be blown off course, or you may need to move to avoid an obstacle on the road.
Q0068 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When you drive and you have a learner licence, do you need to have your licence with you?
  • [A] Yes ✔ Correct
  • [B] No
Explanation: Yes, you must always have your licence with you when you drive.
Q0069 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Can a police officer impound your car on the spot if you`re caught driving while disqualified?
  • [A] Yes ✔ Correct
  • [B] Only if there is another driver with a licence in the vehicle
  • [C] No. They must get a impound order
Explanation: If you are driving with a suspended licence, no licence, or if you have an expired licence and have been forbidden to drive then a police officer can impound your vehicle on the spot. You could face court-imposed penalties and your vehicle could be impounded for 28 days.
Q0070 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Before you turn to the right on a straight road, what must you do? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Signal for at least three seconds ✔ Correct
  • [B] Give way to vehicles from the left
  • [C] Give way to vehicles coming straight ahead
  • [D] Move towards the centre line
  • [E] E. Check your mirrors
Explanation: Before you turn to the right you must signal for three seconds after you have checked your mirrors. Then move towards the centre line and give way to vehicles coming towards you.
Q0071 All Classes Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you do if your vehicle has a current warrant of fitness but a rear red stop light is not working?
  • [A] You can wait until your next WoF to get it fixed
  • [B] You must fix it immediately ✔ Correct
  • [C] You can use the vehicle as long as you're not driving at night
Explanation: A police officer may pull you over and has the authority to fine you as you should not be driving a defective car.
Q0072 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When vehicles pass a school bus that has stopped to let children on or off, what is the speed limit permitted for the passing vehicle?
  • [A] 20kph ✔ Correct
  • [B] 25kph
  • [C] 35kph
  • [D] 50kph
Explanation: One must slow down to 20kph if a school bus is letting children off, regardless of the direction you are approaching. A child could dash in front of the school bus which is why you need to slow down.
Q0073 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What does this marking mean?
  • [A] Fire station
  • [B] 1 hour parking permitted
  • [C] Bus lane ahead
  • [D] Fire hydrant ✔ Correct
Explanation: A location of a fire hydrant is marked.
Q0074 All Classes Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Can you carry passengers if you have a learner licence?
  • [A] No
  • [B] Yes
  • [C] Yes, but only if a supervisor agrees to it ✔ Correct
Explanation: If the person supervising agrees to it then you can carry passengers in your car. They will be responsible for the passengers and your actions while driving.
Q0075 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When must you turn your vehicle headlights on?
  • [A] 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise
  • [B] In fog
  • [C] You can't see 100metres ahead of you
  • [D] All of the above ✔ Correct
Explanation: Using your lights will make you more visible, as in all of these situations your vehicle is less visible to other drivers. If your motorcycle was manufactured after 1 January 1980, it is mandatory that you turn your headlights or daytime running lights on during daylight hours.
Q0076 All Classes Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
A Warrant of Fitness shows what? Select all that apply.
  • [A] The vehicle is safe to be on the road
  • [B] An approved WoF inspector has inspected the vehicle ✔ Correct
  • [C] The month the WoF expires
Explanation: It's the driver's responsibility to ensure that the vehicle they are driving is safe and roadworthy at all times. The WoF label shows the month it was expected and the expiry and proves that the vehicle was roadworthy at time of inspection.
Q0077 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
The headlights on your vehicle MUST be dipped at what time? Check all those that apply.
  • [A] when you are behind other vehicles ✔ Correct
  • [B] when a police officer is directing traffic
  • [C] when you park
  • [D] when other vehicles are approaching you
Explanation: All the options are mandatory. There are other examples where you might dip your lights, such as driving in fog or driving when there is enough light.
Q0078 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
You must check that there is space for your vehicle on the other side of the line when driving across a railway level crossing? True or false?
  • [A] TRUE ✔ Correct
  • [B] FALSE
  • [C] Only on crossings that don't have signals and/or barrier arms
Explanation: When a train is coming, you must check that there's enough room to get your vehicle across or you may be stranded on the lines.
Q0079 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you do when you come to a pedestrian crossing with a raised traffic island in the centre?
  • [A] If a pedestrian is on your half of the crossing then stop and give way ✔ Correct
  • [B] If a pedestrian is on any part of the crossing then stop and give way.
Explanation: Yes , as long as it's safe to do so you can continue driving through the crossing if a pedestrian is not either crossing or waiting to cross on your side.
Q0080 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When can you use your horn? Select all that apply.
  • [A] To warn another driver of your presence ✔ Correct
  • [B] To warn a motorcycle that you are approaching
  • [C] If you're made because someone cuts in front of you
  • [D] To say good-bye as you leave your family's house
Explanation: Your horn should only be used for a reasonable traffic warning.
Q0081 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
In a 50kph zone and not in an emergency when must you not use the horn on your vehicle?
  • [A] After midnight and before 8am
  • [B] Between 4:30pm and 6:30pm
  • [C] Any time you are near a hospital or in a school zone
  • [D] Between 3pm and 5pm
  • [E] E. Between 11pm and 7am ✔ Correct
Explanation: In an urban zone (50kph area) between 11pm and 7am is the only time you should use your horn for an emergency.
Q0082 All Classes Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
If you have a car licence, can you drive a moped?
  • [A] Yes ✔ Correct
  • [B] No
Explanation: Correct. A moped has an engine less than 50 cc and is a motorbike.
Q0083 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When does a police officer have the power to arrest you? Select all that apply.
  • [A] If you don't come to a stop when required to ✔ Correct
  • [B] If you give false information to the police officer about the ownership of the vehicle you are driving and/or if you fail to provide your name and address
  • [C] If you refuse to have your blood or breath tested for alcohol.
  • [D] If you continue to drive when you have been told not to drive by a police officer
  • [E] E. If you fail to hand over your keys to a police officer when requested
Explanation: You did not get all of them. All of these are grounds for a police officer to arrest you.
Q0084 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
A police officer has the power to arrest you at what time? Select all those that apply.
  • [A] If you don't stop when instructed ✔ Correct
  • [B] If you give false vehicle ownership information of the vehicle you are driving or if you refuse to tell the police officer your name and address
  • [C] If you refuse to have your blood or breath tested for alcohol.
  • [D] If you drive when instructed not to be a police officer
  • [E] E. If you refuse to provide your car keys to an officer when requested
Explanation: You missed some. A police officer can arrest you for all of these.
Q0085 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When you hear a siren or see red flashing lights from an ambulance or fire engine, what must you do?
  • [A] If they're driving behind you speed up so you're not slowing them down
  • [B] Stop where you are immediately
  • [C] Slow down and pull over to allow them to pass. Stop if necessary ✔ Correct
  • [D] Slow down and pull your car up on the footpath
Explanation: You must slow down and pull over if they are behind you and you must stop if necessary. If a police car is following you with its lights flashing, then you must stop. A police car will have blue and red lights.
Q0086 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Select the options in which a horn can be used.
  • [A] To let another driver know that you are there ✔ Correct
  • [B] To alert a rider on their horse that you are approaching
  • [C] If you're angry and upset at someone because they took your parking space
  • [D] As you drop off your kids at school
Explanation: A horn should only be used for a traffic warning.
Q0087 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
How should an entrance way into a public car park be treated, for the purpose of applying the Give Way rule?
  • [A] As an intersection ✔ Correct
  • [B] As a driveway
  • [C] The vehicle that is there first has right of way
  • [D] As a one-way street
Explanation: The Give Way rules are as follows: * If you are turning right at an intersection, give way to vehicles proceeding towards you that are turning left. * Give way to all vehicles that aren't turning, if you are turning at an intersection. * In all other situations, give way to all...
Q0088 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
The two-second rule has what purpose? Check any that apply.
  • [A] Overtaking vehicles are able to move back into the line of traffic safely if required
  • [B] To give you enough time to stop if the vehicle in front stops ✔ Correct
  • [C] If required two seconds is enough time to stop in any weather conditions.
Explanation: The two-second rule should be applied to assist you in stopping safely only if it's dry weather. In wet weather, you should apply the four-second rule. As regards overtaking, a vehicle should not overtake if the manoeuvre cannot be completed safely.
Q0089 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
If you want to turn right at traffic signals where a green light is showing, what must you do?
  • [A] Give way to vehicles coming towards you ✔ Correct
  • [B] Give way to cars coming from the left
  • [C] Give way to cars coming from the right
  • [D] Wait and turn when the light turns red
Explanation: Give way to drivers coming towards you, The Give Way rules apply here .
Q0090 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Within how many hours of a crash does the driver need to tell a police officer if somebody is hurt?
  • [A] Within 24 hours ✔ Correct
  • [B] Within 2 days
  • [C] Within 36 hrs
  • [D] Just make sure the injured people are OK- no need to report it to police
Explanation: In any case it must be reported as soon as possible and within 24 hrs.
Q0091 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When you see red flashing lights from an ambulance, a fire engine, or when you hear a siren, what must you do?
  • [A] If they're driving behind you speed up so you're not slowing them down
  • [B] Stop where you are immediately
  • [C] Slow down and pull over to allow them to pass. Stop if necessary ✔ Correct
  • [D] Slow down and pull your car up on the footpath
Explanation: You must slow down and pull over if they are behind you and you must stop if necessary. If a police car is following you with its lights flashing, then you must stop. A police car will have blue and red lights.
Q0092 All Classes Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
With a car licence can you drive a moped?
  • [A] Yes ✔ Correct
  • [B] No
Explanation: Correct. You can drive a moped on a car licence, it's a motorbike with an engine less than 50cc.
Q0093 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
If yellow traffic signals are flashing, what does it mean?
  • [A] Apply the give way rules as the traffic signals are faulty ✔ Correct
  • [B] If pedestrians have finished crossing then you can proceed through the intersection
  • [C] Prepare to stop- a wide load is coming through the intersection
  • [D] An accident has just happened
Explanation: Correct. Proceed with caution and apply the give way rules as there is something wrong with the lights. However, if a police officer is directing traffic then you would follow their signals instead.
Q0094 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
You must be able to stop in half the length of clear road you can see in front of you when driving at night on a road with lanes. True or false?
  • [A] TRUE
  • [B] False. ✔ Correct
  • [C] Only when driving conditions are poor
Explanation: You must be able to stop the length of clear road you can see in front of you on a road with lanes. On a road without lanes, you must be able to stop in half the distance you can see in front of you.
Q0095 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
In a 50kph zone (unless in an emergency), when must not use the horn on your vehicle?
  • [A] Between 8am and 5pm
  • [B] Between 3pm and 6pm
  • [C] Any time you are in a school zone
  • [D] Between midnight and 6am
  • [E] E. Between 11pm and 7am ✔ Correct
Explanation: Between 11pm and 7am in an urban zone (50kph area) is the only time you should use your horn for an emergency.
Q0096 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Flashing yellow traffic signals are an indicator of what?
  • [A] Apply the give way rules as the traffic signals are faulty ✔ Correct
  • [B] If pedestrians have finished crossing then you can proceed through the intersection
  • [C] Prepare to stop-wide load is coming through the junction
  • [D] A crash has occurred
Explanation: Proceed with caution and apply the give way rules, as there is something wrong with their lights. However, if police are directing traffic then follow their signals.
Q0097 All Classes Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Do you have to have your learner licence with you when you are driving as a learner?
  • [A] Yes ✔ Correct
  • [B] No
Explanation: Yes, you must always have your licence with you when you drive.
Q0098 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
A school bus has stopped to let children on or off, what is the speed limit for vehicles passing?
  • [A] 20kph ✔ Correct
  • [B] 25kph
  • [C] 30kph
  • [D] 35kph
Explanation: You must slow down to 20kph if a school bus is letting children off, regardless of the direction you are approaching.
Q0099 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When should you turn your vehicle headlights on?
  • [A] 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise
  • [B] In fog
  • [C] When you can't see 100 metres ahead of you
  • [D] All of the above ✔ Correct
Explanation: Using your lights will make you more visible, all of these situations mean your vehicle is less visible to other road users. Note that it is mandatory to turn your headlights or daytime running lights on during daylight hours if you are riding a motorbike that was manufactured...
Q0100 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When red lights are flashing at a railway level crossing, what should you do?
  • [A] Look both ways and cross if there are no trains coming
  • [B] Remain stopped until the lights are no longer flashing ✔ Correct
  • [C] As soon as the train has passed you can go
Explanation: Even if a train has already passed, you must stop when lights are flashing at a railway level crossing, as there may be another train coming.
Q0101 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Which vehicle must give way if two vehicles are facing Give Way signs?
  • [A] Whichever vehicle gets there last
  • [B] Whichever vehicle isn't turning
  • [C] The vehicle that is turning ✔ Correct
  • [D] Whichever vehicle is larger
Explanation: The vehicle that is turning has to give way. If one vehicle is turning left and the other turning right, the vehicle turning right gives way. If both vehicles are turning right or left, there should be no need to give way, as you won't cross paths.
Q0102 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When MUST you always dip your headlights on your vehicle at night? Check all that apply.
  • [A] When other vehicles are driving towards you ✔ Correct
  • [B] When you are following other vehicles
  • [C] When traffic is being directed by a police officer
  • [D] When you park your car
  • [E] E. When you are backing out of a driveway
Explanation: Correct. A, B, C, and D are all examples of when you must dip your headlights. You don't need to dip your headlights if there's no danger of you A, B, C or D happening while you are performing a reversing manoeuvre.
Q0103 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Who is responsible for making a child under 15 years old (0-14), use a safety belt or a safety seat in a vehicle?
  • [A] The person whose had their licence the longest
  • [B] The driver ✔ Correct
  • [C] The passenger
  • [D] The oldest person in the car
Explanation: All passengers under 15 years of age are held under the responsibility of the driver for seatbelts. Any passengers that are older then 15 are responsible for putting their own seatbelts on.
Q0104 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you do to prevent being blinded by the headlights of an oncoming vehicle?
  • [A] Let the other driver know by flashing your lights
  • [B] Slow down and keep your eyes to the left of the road ✔ Correct
  • [C] Keep your eyes to the right-hand side of the road
  • [D] Look at the dotted yellow line
Explanation: Keep your eyes to the left to ensure you won't be looking directly into the light. You could cause an accident if you flash your lights at the other driver as it risks blinding or distracting them. Your forward visibility will be reduced so be sure to slow down.
Q0105 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
If you are driving in fog, which of your vehicle's lights do you have on?
  • [A] Park lights (side lights)
  • [B] Front and rear fog lights
  • [C] Dipped headlights
  • [D] All of the above ✔ Correct
Explanation: Don't use full beam headlights, as it can reflect back at you and reduce your visibility, but you can use all of your other lights in the fog. Keep your headlights dipped and turn your fog lights off when the fog passes to avoid dazzling other drivers.
Q0106 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What must you do when you approach a pedestrian crossing with a raised traffic island in the middle?
  • [A] If a pedestrian is on your side of the crossing then stop and give way ✔ Correct
  • [B] If the pedestrian is on any part of the crossing then stop and give way
Explanation: Yes, as long as it is safe to do so and the pedestrian is not crossing or waiting to cross on your side then you can carry on through the crossing.
Q0107 All Classes Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What is the maximum distance allowed between two vehicles if you tow another vehicle?
  • [A] 2m
  • [B] 4m ✔ Correct
  • [C] 6m
  • [D] 8m
Explanation: Between the rear of the vehicle being towed and the front of the vehicle being towed, the maximum distance is 4m.
Q0108 All Classes Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
You must always drive with a supervisor when you have a learner licence. What is a supervisor?
  • [A] A person over the age of 25 with a full New Zealand driver's licence of the same class that you are driving
  • [B] A person who has held a full New Zealand driver's licence for more than two years in the same class that you are driving ✔ Correct
  • [C] A driver that has had a restricted licence for at least a year in any class and that is 25 or older
  • [D] A person over the age of 25 who has held any New Zealand driver's licence for 1 or more years
Explanation: A driver that has held a New Zealand's full Class 1 driver licence for two or more years.
Q0109 All Classes Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Before any modification is carried out on your vehicle what should you do?
  • [A] As long as you purchase your parts from a reputable dealer then it is OK to modify your vehicle
  • [B] Check with a warrant of fitness inspector ✔ Correct
  • [C] Get a certificate from your lawyer
  • [D] Indicate the modification on your vehicle registration papers
Explanation: It's best to check with a WoF inspector before modifying your vehicle in any way, that way you won't be creating a problem for yourself in the future.
Q0110 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Your vehicle headlights must be turned on when visibility is less than:
  • [A] 50 metres
  • [B] 100 metres ✔ Correct
  • [C] 200 metres
  • [D] 250 metres
Explanation: You need to turn your lights on if you can't see a person within 100 metres.
Q0111 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Should you pull over and stop if you see a police car with its red and blue lights flashing behind you?
  • [A] Yes ✔ Correct
  • [B] No
Explanation: Yes, however if the police car continues on it's way and passes by you, then you don't need to stop.
Q0112 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
You can be required to undergo a breath screen test by who?
  • [A] A police officer ✔ Correct
  • [B] A fire officer
  • [C] A lawyer
  • [D] A nurse
  • [E] E. None of the above
Explanation: A police officer will ask you to blow into either a tube of crystals with a bag on the end or a small electronic device. If your alcohol level is high, you will be asked to take an evidential breath test or have a blood test.
Q0113 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
From the time you pass a crash site to the time you pass an Accident sign, what is the speed limit?
  • [A] 20kph ✔ Correct
  • [B] 30kph
  • [C] 45kph
  • [D] 55kph
Explanation: Correct. 20kph is the safest speed, as there might be police on the scene and debris on the road.
Q0114 All Classes Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
If you have a space saver wheel fitted, what is the maximum speed you may drive?
  • [A] 70kph
  • [B] 80kph ✔ Correct
  • [C] 90kph
  • [D] 100kph
Explanation: On a space saver tyre, 80kph is the maximum speed allowed.
Q0115 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
From the time you pass an Accident sign until you have passed the crash site, what is the speed limit?
  • [A] 20kph ✔ Correct
  • [B] 35kph
  • [C] 45kph
  • [D] 60kph
Explanation: 20 kph is the safest speed, as there may be debris and police still on scene.
Q0116 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When red lights are flashing at a railway level crossing, what should you do?
  • [A] Look both ways and cross if there are no trains coming
  • [B] Remain stopped until the lights are no longer flashing ✔ Correct
  • [C] As soon as the train has passed you can go.
Explanation: Even if a train has already passed, you must stop when lights are flashing at a railway level crossing, there may be another train coming.
Q0117 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When is it permitted to pass a vehicle to its left? Check all that apply.
  • [A] You have been directed to by a police officer ✔ Correct
  • [B] It's safe to pass as there are two or more lanes on your side of the road
  • [C] The car you will pass is signalling a right turn and is either slowing down or has stopped
  • [D] There's enough room to pass safely on a signal lane road and the vehicle is a motorbike or scooter
Explanation: The correct answers are A, B and C. When passing motorbikes and scooters you must maintain a safe distance as they can easily be blown off course, or may need to move to avoid an obstacle on the road.
Q0118 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What is a courtesy crossing?
  • [A] It's a crossing that is controlled by red or green flashing lights
  • [B] It's at crossing lights where a yellow man symbol appears to allow pedestrians to cross the road
  • [C] It's not a required stop, it's a raised crossing in the road that allows a safe place for pedestrians to cross. ✔ Correct
Explanation: Although they are not official pedestrian crossings, they do provide a safe spot for drivers to stop and allow pedestrians to cross. Normally they are made out of bricks or paving and are above the road level.
Q0119 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When driving are you required to carry your licence at all times if you are the holder of any class of driver licence?
  • [A] No
  • [B] Yes ✔ Correct
  • [C] Only if you're on a suspended licence
Explanation: Regardless of the type of licence you have, you must carry your driver licence at all times when driving.
Q0120 All Classes Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When can you carry passengers with a restricted licence? Check all that apply.
  • [A] At any time, as long as a supervisor with a full driver's licence is sitting in the front passenger seat (the supervisor must have had the licence for at least 2 years) ✔ Correct
  • [B] Between 5am and 10pm, as long as your passengers are your own children or your spouse/de facto partner
  • [C] Only between 8am and 9pm
  • [D] Only if your car has five or more seats
Explanation: If the passengers are your spouse/de facto partner, your children, a relative who lives with you and is a beneficiary, or someone for whom you are the primary caregiver then you can carry them without a supervisor between 5am and 10pm. If you have a supervisor with a full...
Q0121 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
You are required to give a blood sample, who is legally allowed to have you take one?
  • [A] A fire officer
  • [B] A police officer ✔ Correct
  • [C] A doctor
  • [D] None of the above
Explanation: An approved person or medical doctor will take the blood sample, but it is a police officer that can require you to give blood if you refuse an evidential breath test. If you don't comply you may be arrested.
Q0122 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Should you pull over and stop if you see a police car with its red and blue lights flashing behind you?
  • [A] Yes ✔ Correct
  • [B] No
Explanation: Yes, but if the police car overtakes you and continues to drive then you are not required to stop.
Q0123 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Before you make a turn to the right, what must you do? Select all that apply.
  • [A] Before you move towards the centre line, slow down ✔ Correct
  • [B] Check your mirrors and your blind spot
  • [C] Signal for at least two seconds
  • [D] Give way to oncoming traffic and traffic that's turning left
  • [E] E. Be aware of your vehicle's swept path
Explanation: You should slow down, check your blind spots, indicate for at least three seconds, position your vehicle near the centre line, give way to other vehicles, and be aware of the path your vehicle and any trailers will take.
Q0124 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Within how many hours of a crash does the driver need to tell a police officer if somebody is hurt?
  • [A] Within 24 hours ✔ Correct
  • [B] Within 48 hours
  • [C] Within 12 hours
  • [D] You don't need to tell the police, you just need to make sure the injured people are OK
Explanation: It must be reported within 24 hours to police, but as soon as possible is best.
Q0125 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
You MUST dip the headlights on your vehicle when? Select all that apply.
  • [A] You are following other vehicles ✔ Correct
  • [B] There is a police officer directing traffic
  • [C] You are parking your vehicle
  • [D] Other vehicles are coming towards you
Explanation: You must dip your headlights in all of these examples. When driving when there is adequate light, such as when there are streetlights, and also in fog where full beam lights make it harder to see would also be scenarios where you would dip your headlights.
Q0126 All Classes Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
How often must you renew its warrant of fitness, if your car was first registered before 1st of January 2000?
  • [A] Three weeks
  • [B] Six months ✔ Correct
  • [C] 2 years
  • [D] 1 year
Explanation: After an initial inspection, another WoF inspection won't be required until the 3rd anniversary of their first registration for all new vehicles. From 1 July 2014, vehicles first registered anywhere in the world on or after 1 January 2000 move to annual WoFs for the lifetime of...
Q0127 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When you're driving past a school bus that has stopped to let children on or of, what is the speed limit?
  • [A] 20kph ✔ Correct
  • [B] 30kph
  • [C] 40kph
  • [D] 50kph
Explanation: You must slow down to 20kph if a school bus is dropping children off, no matter the direction you are approaching. This is in case a child runs across the road.
Q0128 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What does it mean if there are one or more yellow flashing lights at traffic signals?
  • [A] Emergency vehicles are coming, all cars must come to a stop
  • [B] The lights are faulty and the Give Way rules apply ✔ Correct
  • [C] There's a diversion ahead
  • [D] Pull over to the right hand side of the road
  • [E] E. Continue driving at the same speed
Explanation: Use the Give Way rules for that intersection and be courteous to other drivers as the lights are 'on the blink.'
Q0129 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
You are allowed to pass a vehicle to your left at what point? Check all that apply.
  • [A] You have been directed to by a police officer ✔ Correct
  • [B] It's safe to pass and there are two or more lanes on your side of the road
  • [C] The car you will pass is either slowing down or has stopped and is signalling a right turn
  • [D] There isn't enough room to pass safely on a single lane road as the vehicle is either a motorcycle or scooter
Explanation: The correct answers are A, B and C. When you pass motorbikes and scooters you must maintain a safe distance as they can easily be blown off course, or you may need to move to avoid an obstacle on the road.
Q0130 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you do if you are turning at traffic lights and there is a red arrow pointing to the right?
  • [A] Stop until you get a green arrow, then continue if it's safe to go
  • [B] Stop until the red arrow disappears and you receive a green traffic light, then continue with the Give Way rules
  • [C] Both a and b are correct ✔ Correct
Explanation: Both examples are correct.
Q0131 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What does 'speed limit' mean?
  • [A] The minimum speed for that road
  • [B] The maximum speed for that road in good conditions ✔ Correct
  • [C] The maximum speed for cars only
  • [D] Except for when overtaking another vehicle it is the maximum speed that you can drive
Explanation: If conditions are good, it is the maximum speed you can drive on that particular road.
Q0132 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What does a Warrant of Fitness show? Select all that apply.
  • [A] The vehicle is safe to be on the road
  • [B] An approved WoF inspector has inspected the vehicle ✔ Correct
  • [C] The month the WoF expires
Explanation: It's the driver's responsibility to ensure that the vehicle they are driving is safe and roadworthy at all times. The WoF label shows the month it was expected and the expiry and proves that the vehicle was roadworthy at time of inspection.
Q0133 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
You must give way to all vehicles that will cross your path from the left when coming up to a roundabout? True or False.
  • [A] TRUE
  • [B] False. ✔ Correct
Explanation: False. Like in the diagram, you don't give way to vehicles coming from your left, you give way to vehicles coming from your right.
Q0134 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
If yellow traffic signals are flashing what does that mean?
  • [A] Apply the give way rules as the traffic signals are faulty ✔ Correct
  • [B] If pedestrians have finished crossing then you can proceed through the intersection.
  • [C] Prepare to stop- a wide load is coming through the intersection
  • [D] An accident has just happened
Explanation: Correct. Proceed with caution and apply the give way rules as there is something wrong with the lights. However, if a police officer is directing traffic then you would follow their signals instead.
Q0135 All Classes Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
If your vehicle is on the road and not up to warrant and fitness standard, can you be fined?
  • [A] Yes ✔ Correct
  • [B] No
Explanation: Yes, you can be fined by a police officer if something appears to be not up to warrant of fitness standard.
Q0136 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When you are turning to the right when must you signal?
  • [A] Only if other traffic is following or approaching you
  • [B] Always, and for at least five seconds before you turn
  • [C] Always, and for at least three seconds before you turn ✔ Correct
Explanation: A safe time to signal for is three seconds as it gives plenty of time for other road users to understand your intentions.
Q0137 All Classes Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

  • [A] The person who has had their license the longest in the car
  • [B] The driver
  • [C] The passenger ✔ Correct
  • [D] Whoever owns the car
Explanation: If the passenger is over 15 they are responsible. The driver is only responsible for passengers under the age of 15.
Q0138 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Before you pass another vehicle, how long should you signal for?
  • [A] One second
  • [B] Four seconds
  • [C] Three seconds ✔ Correct
  • [D] If there is another vehicle coming towards you or one coming behind you then you need to signal
Explanation: You should signal for a minimum of 3 seconds. This gives the vehicles behind you enough time to see your intention and provides you with enough time to ensure that the road ahead is safe and clear.
Q0139 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
On a sealed road at a Give Way sign, what is the colour of the painted line?
  • [A] Yellow
  • [B] Blue
  • [C] White ✔ Correct
Explanation: The line is white.
Q0140 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When you are at an intersection, what do a police officer's directions overrule?
  • [A] Traffic lights
  • [B] Give Way rules
  • [C] Road signs, such as stop signs
  • [D] All of the above ✔ Correct
Explanation: All other signs and signals at an intersection are overruled by a police officer's directions.
Q0141 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What does 'speed limit' mean?
  • [A] The ideal speed for that road
  • [B] In good conditions, it is the maximum driving speed for that road ✔ Correct
  • [C] The minimum speed for that road in good conditions
  • [D] The maximum driving speed during the summer months
Explanation: If road conditions are good the speed limit is the maximum speed in which you can drive on that road.
Q0142 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
You must give way to all vehicles that will cross your path from your left when coming up to a roundabout? True or False?
  • [A] TRUE
  • [B] FALSE ✔ Correct

Q0143 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

  • [A] If you don't stop when requested ✔ Correct
  • [B] If you give false information about the ownership of the vehicle you are driving or if you refuse to tell the police officer your name and address
  • [C] If you refuse blood or breath alcohol testing
  • [D] If you continue to drive after you have been told not to by a police officer

Q0144 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

  • [A] Check both ways and wait until they are no longer flashing to cross ✔ Correct

Q0145 All Classes Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

  • [C] A driver that has had a restricted licence for at least a year in any class and that is 25 or older

Q0146 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
The four-second rule should be applied when?

  • [C] If you’re driving faster than 90kph
  • [D] Night time driving
Explanation: Use the four-second rule as wet and frosty roads can double the stopping distance. The extra weight of a trailer will also add to your stopping distance.
Q0147 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

  • [A] 1m ✔ Correct

Q0148 All Classes Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

  • [A] The vehicle is safe to be on the road
  • [B] An approved WoF inspector has inspected the vehicle ✔ Correct
  • [C] The month the WoF expires
Explanation: It's the driver's responsibility to ensure that the vehicle they are driving is safe and roadworthy at all times. The WoF label shows the month it was expected and the expiry and proves that the vehicle was roadworthy at time of inspection.
Q0149 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What does it mean if at traffic signals there are one or more yellow flashing lights?
  • [A] Emergency vehicles are coming, all cars must come to a stop.

  • [C] There's a diversion ahead

Q0150 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

  • [B] If your back brakes are worn out
  • [C] When your overtaking
  • [D] At night
Explanation: Use the four-second rule when driving on wet and frosty road as they can double stopping distance. A trailer and the extra weight will also add to your stopping distance.
Q0151 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When driving a car in wet or frosty conditions what rule should you use to judge a safe following distance?
  • [A] Two-second rule
  • [B] Four-second rule ✔ Correct
  • [C] 200 metre rule
Explanation: You need to observe the four-second rule as it can take up to twice as long to stop in such weather conditions. This rule also applies anytime that you are towing a trailer.
Q0152 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

  • [A] Two-second rule

Q0153 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

Q0155 All Classes Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

Q0158 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

Q0160 All Classes Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Car tyres require what minimum depth for their treads?
  • [A] 1mm

  • [A] Yes ✔ Correct

Q0162 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

  • [D] Look at the line in the middle of the road

Q0166 All Classes Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

Q0167 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

  • [A] Give way to vehicles coming towards you ✔ Correct

  • [E] E. Continue driving at the same speed

  • [A] Fire officer

  • [C] Police officer ✔ Correct
  • [D] Taxi Cab driver
Explanation: If something appears wrong with your vehicle then a police officer may be required to stop you for a vehicle check.
Q0187 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What is the purpose of the two-second rule. Check any that apply.
  • [A] To allow overtaking vehicles to move back into the line of traffic safely if required
  • [B] If the vehicle stops in front it gives you enough time to stop ✔ Correct
  • [C] If required two seconds is enough time to stop in any weather conditions.
Explanation: The purpose of the two-second rule is to allow you to stop safely in dry weather. Apply the four-second rule if it's wet. A vehicle should not overtake if the manoeuvre cannot be completed safely.
Q0188 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When passing another vehicle how long should you signal for?
  • [A] One second
  • [B] Four seconds
  • [C] Three seconds ✔ Correct
  • [D] If there is another vehicle coming towards you or one coming behind you then you need to signal
Explanation: You should signal for a minimum of 3 seconds, as it gives the vehicles behind you enough time to see your intention and provides you with enough time to ensure that the road ahead is safe and clear.
Q0189 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Legally who may require you to give a blood sample?
  • [A] An ambulance officer
  • [B] A police officer ✔ Correct
  • [C] A lawyer
  • [D] None of the above
Explanation: A medical doctor or other approved professional will take the blood sample, but it is the police officer who can require you to give the sample. You may be arrested if you don't comply and refuse an evidential breath test.
Q0190 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What hours can you drive on your own if you have a restricted licence?
  • [A] 10pm-5am ✔ Correct
  • [B] Dawn to dusk
  • [C] 5am-6pm
  • [D] 5am-9pm
Explanation: Correct. You can drive on your own on a restricted licence, as long as you have someone with you from 10pm to 5am.
Q0191 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Who can enforce a breath screening test?
  • [A] A police officer ✔ Correct
  • [B] A fire officer
  • [C] A lawyer
  • [D] A doctor
  • [E] E. None of the above
Explanation: You will be asked to blow into either a small electronic device or a tube of crystals with a bag at the end by a police officer. You will be asked to take an evidential breath or blood test if your alcohol level is too high.
Q0192 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Which vehicle gives way if two vehicles are facing Give Way signs?
  • [A] Whichever vehicle gets there last
  • [B] The vehicle that is not turning
  • [C] The vehicle that is turning ✔ Correct
  • [D] Whichever is the larger vehicle
Explanation: A vehicle that is turning has to give way. If one vehicle is turning right and the other is turning left, the vehicle turning right gives way. There should be no need to give way, if both vehicles are turning right or left as you won't cross paths.
Q0193 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
You must be able to stop in half the length of clear road you can see in front of you when driving at night on a road with lanes. True or false?
  • [A] TRUE
  • [B] FALSE ✔ Correct
  • [C] Only when it's wet
Explanation: You must be able to stop in the length of clear road you can see in front of you on a road with lanes; on a road without lanes you must be able to stop in half the distance you can see in front of you.
Q0194 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What must you do when approaching a pedestrian crossing without a raised traffic island?
  • [A] If a pedestrian is on your half of the crossing then stop and give way
  • [B] Stop and give way if a pedestrian is on any part of the crossing ✔ Correct
  • [C] There's no raised island so you can continue driving, the responsibility is on the pedestrian to ensure that the road is safe.
Explanation: You must stop when the pedestrian is on any part of the crossing if the crossing doesn't have a central raised traffic island.
Q0195 All Classes Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

  • [B] Between 5am and 10pm, as long as your passengers are your own children or your spouse/de facto partner
  • [C] Only between 8am and 9pm
  • [D] Only if your car has five or more seats

Q0196 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Can a police officer impound your car on the spot if you're caught driving while disqualified?
  • [A] Yes ✔ Correct
  • [B] Only if you are under the influence of alcohol
  • [C] No. They must have an impound order.

Q0197 All Classes Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Before any modification is carried out on your vehicle, what should you do?
  • [A] As long as you purchase your parts from a reputable dealer then it is OK to modify your vehicle
  • [B] Check with a warrant of fitness inspector ✔ Correct
  • [C] Get a certificate from your lawyer
  • [D] Indicate the modification on your vehicle registration papers
Explanation: It's best to check with a WoF inspector before modifying your vehicle in any way, that way you won't be creating a problem for yourself in the future.
Q0198 All Classes Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
A load may extend in front of a car a maximum distance of what?
  • [A] 1.5m from behind the bumper
  • [B] 3m in front of the front edge of the front seat ✔ Correct
  • [C] Nowhere behind the bumper
  • [D] 3.5m in front of the bumper
Explanation: One can carry a load that extends 3m in front of the front edge of the front seat and that extends 4m behind the rear axle.
Q0199 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When should you be using your horn? Select all those that apply.
  • [A] To let another drive know that you are there ✔ Correct
  • [B] To warn a motorcycle
  • [C] If someone cuts in front of you
  • [D] As you are leaving a family member's house
Explanation: To provide a reasonable traffic warning is the only time you should use your horn.
Q0200 All Classes Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Who is legally allowed to stop you and perform a roadside check on your vehicle? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Fire officer
  • [B] Ambulance officer
  • [C] Police officer ✔ Correct
  • [D] Taxi Cab driver
Explanation: If something appears wrong with your vehicle, then a police officer may be required to stop you for a vehicle check.
Q0201 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When MUST you always dip your headlights on your vehicle at night? Check all that apply.
  • [A] When other vehicles are driving towards you ✔ Correct
  • [B] When you are following other vehicles
  • [C] When traffic is being directed by a police officer
  • [D] When you park your car
  • [E] E. When you are backing out of a driveway
Explanation: Correct. A, B, C, and D are all examples of when you must dip your headlights. You don't need to dip your headlights if there's no danger of you A, B, C or D happening while you are performing a reversing manoeuvre.
Q0202 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
A roadside check can be performed by who legally? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Fire officer
  • [B] Licenced Mechanic
  • [C] Police officer ✔ Correct
  • [D] Member of council
Explanation: If something appears wrong with your vehicle then a police offer may require you to stop for a vehicle check.
Q0203 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
If you are going straight through a roundabout, don't signal as you come up to the roundabout, only signal left as you pass the exit before the one you wish to take. True or false?
  • [A] TRUE ✔ Correct
  • [B] FALSE
Explanation: True. You may not be able to give the required three seconds of indication on a smaller roundabout, but you still must indicate.
Q0204 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What does this marking mean?
  • [A] Electric and hybrid vehicles can be charged there
  • [B] Buses only parking
  • [C] A bus lane is ahead
  • [D] Fire hydrant ✔ Correct
Explanation: The location of a fire hydrant is marked.
Q0205 All Classes Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
If your vehicle is on the road and not up to warrant and fitness standard can you be fined?
  • [A] Yes ✔ Correct
  • [B] No
Explanation: Yes, you can be fined by a police officer if something appears to be not up to warrant of fitness standard.
Q0206 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When does the four-second rule need to be applied?
  • [A] If the road is wet or frosty, or you are towing a trailer ✔ Correct
  • [B] If you have worn out brakes
  • [C] If you're travelling at more than 80kph
  • [D] When it gets dark out
Explanation: The four-second rule should be used on wet and frosty roads, as they can double the stopping distance. The extra weight of a trailer will also add to your stopping distance.
Q0207 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
You must check that there is space for your vehicle on the other side of the line when driving across a railway level crossing. True or false?
  • [A] TRUE ✔ Correct
  • [B] False.
  • [C] Only on crossings that don't have signals and/or barrier arms
Explanation: When a train is coming you must check there's enough room to get your vehicle across or you may be stranded on the lines.
Q0208 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Which vehicle lights should you turn on when driving at night?
  • [A] Position lights (park lights) only
  • [B] Dipped headlights (low beam) ✔ Correct
  • [C] High beam lights
  • [D] Fog lights
Explanation: First you should turn on your dipped headlights, which will also turn on your park lights. You can use your high beam headlights and fog lights if the situation arises, and you can leave your position lights on while you are parked and in the vehicle.
Q0209 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When you're turning to the right, when must you signal?
  • [A] Only if other traffic is behind you or approaching you
  • [B] Always, and for at least two seconds before you turn
  • [C] Always, and for at least three seconds before you turn ✔ Correct
Explanation: In order to give plenty of time for other road users to understand your intentions give three seconds for a safe signal time.
Q0210 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Which vehicle gives way if both vehicles are facing Give Way signs?
  • [A] Whichever car gets there first
  • [B] The car that isn't turning
  • [C] That car that is turning ✔ Correct
  • [D] The largest vehicle
Explanation: If both cars are turning in the same direction there should be no need to give way as you won't cross paths. A vehicle that is turning has to give way. If one vehicle is turning left and the other turning right, the vehicle turning right gives way.
Q0211 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
