  • [A] It's a crossing that is controlled by red or green flashing lights
  • [B] It's at crossing lights where a yellow man symbol appears to allow pedestrians to cross the road
  • [C] It's not a required stop, it's a raised crossing in the road that allows a safe place for pedestrians to cross. ✔ Correct
Explanation: Although they are not official pedestrian crossings, they do provide a safe spot for drivers to stop and allow pedestrians to cross. Normally they are made out of bricks or paving and are above the road level.
Q0212 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When you're at an intersection, when must you not pass a vehicle on the left?
  • [A] When the other car has stopped
  • [B] When the other car is indicating right
  • [C] When the other car is indicating left ✔ Correct
Explanation: You must not pass on the left if a vehicle is indicating left because there is a risk that it will turn into your path.
Q0213 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Within how many hours of a crash does the driver need to tell a police officer is somebody is hurt?
  • [A] Within 24 hours ✔ Correct
  • [B] Within 2 days
  • [C] Within 36 hrs
  • [D] Just make sure the injured people are OK- no need to report it to police
Explanation: In any case it must be reported as soon as possible and within 24 hrs.
Q0214 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

  • [A] When the other car slows down
  • [B] When the other car is indicating right
  • [C] When the other car is indicating left ✔ Correct
Explanation: You must not pass a vehicle on the left that is indicating left because there is a risk it will turn into your path.
Q0215 All Classes Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
The line painted on a sealed road at a Give Way sign is what colour?
  • [A] Blue
  • [B] Yellow
  • [C] White ✔ Correct
Explanation: It's white.
Q0216 All Classes Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
A passenger that is 15 or over is required to put on their safety belt, who is responsible for making them?
  • [A] The person who has had their license the longest in the car
  • [B] The driver
  • [C] The passenger ✔ Correct
  • [D] Whoever owns the car
Explanation: If the passenger is over 15 they are responsible. The driver is only responsible for passengers under the age of 15.

Q0635 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Which of these should you do if you're coming up to a railway level crossing? Check all that apply.

  • [B] Slow down and get ready to stop ✔ Correct
  • [C] Before you cross make sure you've checked both ways
  • [D] If there are no trains coming and nothing blocking your path then you can cross
Explanation: You should be cautious when crossing to ensure that there is no train coming and that you can cross your whole vehicle to the other side. Just because there are no barriers doesn't mean the line isn't used.
Q0636 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

Q0638 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

Q0639 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you do when opening your car door if you look in the mirror and see a cyclist?
  • [A] The cyclist will be able to see you if you open it slowly
  • [B] Open it quickly and try and get out of the way
  • [C] Wait until the cyclist has passed ✔ Correct
  • [D] Toot your horn before you get out to warn the cyclist
Explanation: Before you open the door you should wait for the cyclist to pass. They may be forced into other traffic if they can't move to the right or they may not see you.
Q0640 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

  • [B] Roundabout ✔ Correct

Explanation: This sign means that you should be prepared to give way as you are approaching a roundabout.
Q0641 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

  • [D] The car on the other side of the road turning right ✔ Correct
Explanation: You should be prepared to slow down or stop as the car turning right on the other side of the road may not see the distance between you and car C.
Q0642 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

Q0643 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

  • [C] Stop, unless you are being followed by the police
  • [D] Stop, then go ahead if the road is clear
Explanation: Correct. You must stop, unless you have been directed through by a police officer. Correct.
Q0644 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

  • [A] Check your blind spots ✔ Correct
  • [B] Reduce speed
  • [C] Speed up
  • [D] Tap your brakes to warn the other drivers
Explanation: Correct. Be sure to turn your head over your left shoulder to check your blind spot.
Q0645 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

  • [B] Look over your shoulder
  • [C] Get out and walk around the vehicle

Q0646 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

Explanation: When you change to the left lane, don't drive on the verge and stay on the road. Road sweepers can move debris off the main road surface and moving too far over can cause a puncture. Staying in the middle of your lane isn't required it just makes it more dangerous for the other...
Q0647 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What does this sign mean?
  • [A] Buses are not permitted to park here
  • [B] Buses are permitted to stop here ✔ Correct
  • [C] Buses and taxis are permitted to park here
Explanation: You may be fined if you stop in a bus stop, only buses are permitted to stop.
Q0648 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
If another vehicle is following you closely, what should you do?
  • [A] Make it easier for them to pass by moving to the left and slowing down ✔ Correct
  • [B] Speed up quickly so that you're no longer holding them up

Q0649 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you do when following another vehicle in wet conditions (if you are driving a car)?
  • [A] Observe the two-second rule
  • [B] Observe the four-second rule ✔ Correct
  • [C] Observe the six-second rule
  • [D] Fall back or overtake so that your visibility is not affected by the spray
Explanation: To be safe you should double the normal following distance, which means you should use the four-second rule. Count 4 seconds between a point on the road that the car in front passes until you pass that point. You would increase this time if you're driving a heavy vehicle or...
Q0650 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What is the legal amount of alcohol limit in micrograms per litre of breath if you are 20 or over?
  • [A] 400mcg
  • [B] 350mcg
  • [C] 250mcg ✔ Correct
  • [D] 100mcg
  • [E] E. Zero
Explanation: 250 mcg/litre of breath is the maximum allowable amount, however it is recommended that you don't drink at all before driving as any amount of alcohol can affect your reaction time.
Q0651 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

  • [D] Look ahead of you
  • [E] E. All the above ✔ Correct
Explanation: At intersections you should be extra careful and check all around for other vehicles.
Q0652 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What is the maximum penalty for a first offence if you refuse to give blood for the purposes of an evidential blood alcohol test?
  • [A] Three months in prison, $4500 fine, disqualified for six months or more ✔ Correct
  • [B] $1500 fine, disqualified for six months
  • [C] Disqualified for 6 months
  • [D] If you're a first time offender then there is no punishment
Explanation: Correct. This is a serious offence. You may be sent to prison for up to three months, fined up to $4500 and your licence may be suspended for 6 months.
Q0653 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

  • [C] Look behind you
  • [D] Look in front of you
  • [E] E. All the above ✔ Correct
Explanation: At intersections you should check all around you for other vehicles and you should be extra cautious.
Q0654 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you do if you are driving on a steep, narrow road downhill and a vehicle is coming up the hill?
  • [A] The cars that are going downhill should give way to the vehicles driving uphill ✔ Correct
  • [B] The cars that are moving uphill should give way to the cars moving downhill
Explanation: Correct. This rule ensures the vehicle travelling downhill, where stopping distances are longer, has to pay more attention, even though a vehicle travelling uphill can (all things being equal) stop quicker.
Q0655 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

  • [C] The parked car (C)

Q0656 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

Q0657 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

Q0658 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

Explanation: Doing a U-turn would leave you facing oncoming traffic, and reversing on the hard shoulder is dangerous.
Q0661 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

Explanation: A safe time to signal for is three seconds.
Q0662 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

  • [E] E. Pull over and let the vehicle pass you
Explanation: Slow down so you're not blinded by the dust, which also minimises your chance of a stone flying up and cracking your windscreen. Have your lights on to increase your visibility to other drivers that are coming in another direction.

Explanation: Before you purchase a car you should get a vehicle history report.

Q0674 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

Q0675 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

Q0678 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

  • [C] The left side of a road

Q0684 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

  • [A] Vehicles moving downhill should give way to vehicles moving uphill ✔ Correct
  • [B] Vehicles moving uphill should give way to vehicles moving downhill

Q0686 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
GVM stands for?
  • [A] Generic Vehicle Maintenance

Q0690 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

Q0691 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

Explanation: T2 indicates that only passenger service vehicles, cycles, motorcycles and vehicles carrying at least two people can utilize the transit lane.
Q0759 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Are you allowed to overtake if you are on a three-laned road and there is one lane on your side, and two lanes coming towards you? There is also a dashed white line on your side of the centre line.
  • [A] Yes ✔ Correct
  • [B] No
Q0760 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What does this sign mean?
  • [A] A left-hand bend indicated by the right side of a road marker post ✔ Correct
  • [B] The left side of the road
  • [C] The middle of a road
Explanation: Correct. The right side of the road on a left-hand bend is indicated by this marker.
Q0761 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When you are coming up to traffic signals and the signals change from green to yellow, what should you do?
  • [A] Drive faster to get through the lights
  • [B] Stop if it's safe to do so ✔ Correct
  • [C] Only stop if you are more than 15 metres from the intersection
Explanation: If it's safe to do so you should stop, this will vary according to the car's braking ability, current road conditions, and the ability for vehicles behind you to stop.
Q0762 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you do if you see a pedestrian carrying a white cane across the street?
  • [A] Warn them that you are there by tooting your horn
  • [B] Stop and wait for them to cross ✔ Correct
  • [C] Drive past them
Explanation: You should stop and let them cross as a white cane. This means that the person has impaired vision and may not be able to see your vehicle.
Q0763 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you do before crossing a railway level crossing? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Look right and left up the tracks ✔ Correct
  • [B] Check there's room for your vehicle on the other side of the crossing
  • [C] Ensure there are no barriers or red flashing lights
  • [D] Make sure there's a speed limit sign on the other side of the crossing
Explanation: A, B and C are the correct answers. First off, make sure there is no train coming, then make sure there is room on the crossing for your vehicle so you don't get stranded on the tracks.
Q0764 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When you are driving a car in wet conditions and you are following another vehicle, what should you do?
  • [A] Practice the two-second rule
  • [B] Practice the four-second rule ✔ Correct
  • [C] Practice the six-second rule
  • [D] Try to overtake so that you don't get sprayed
Explanation: You should use the four-second rule and double the normal following distance, to be safe. Count four seconds between a point on the road that the car in front passes until you pass that point. If you're driving a heavy vehicle or towing a large trailer, you should increase this...
Q0765 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Before reversing your vehicle, how would you check for hazards? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Check your rear-view and wing mirrors before reversing ✔ Correct
  • [B] Check over your shoulder
  • [C] Get out of the car and walk around it
  • [D] If your car has reversing sensors or cameras, ensure that they are on
Explanation: These are all acceptable ways to check for hazards before reversing.
Q0766 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
A vehicle is coming up the hill when you are on a narrow, steep road going downhill. What should you do?
  • [A] Vehicles driving downhill should give way to vehicles driving uphill ✔ Correct
  • [B] Vehicles driving uphill should give way to vehicles driving downhill
Explanation: Correct. Although a vehicle driving uphill can ( all things being equal) stop faster, this rule ensures the vehicle driving downhill has to pay more attention where the stopping distances are longer.
Q0767 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Can small amounts of alcohol affect your driving ability?
  • [A] A small amount of alcohol won't impact your driving ability
  • [B] Any amount of alcohol will have some effect on your driving ✔ Correct
Explanation: Drinking small amounts of alcohol can affect your reaction time.
Q0768 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Of the four hazards marked, which one is most likely to require you to take urgent action if you are the driver of the blue car?
  • [A] The parked car
  • [B] The reversing car ✔ Correct
  • [C] The car driving towards you
  • [D] The car parked on the other side of the road
Explanation: The main hazard here is the reversing car. You should be prepared to stop as you may be in the reversing car's blind spot.
Q0769 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you do before crossing a railway level crossing? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Look right and left up the tracks ✔ Correct
  • [B] Check there's room for your vehicle on the other side of the crossing
  • [C] Ensure there are no barriers or red flashing lights
  • [D] Make sure there's a speed limit sign on the other side of the crossing
Explanation: A, b and C are the correct answers. First off, make sure there is no train coming, then make sure there is room on the crossing for your vehicle so you don't get stranded on the tracks.
Q0770 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Of the four hazards marked, which one is most likely to require you to take urgent action if you are the driver of the blue car?
  • [A] The car on the other side of the road turning left
  • [B] The car approaching you
  • [C] The car you are following
  • [D] The car on the other side of the road turning right ✔ Correct
Explanation: You should be prepared to slow down or stop, the car turning right on the other side of the road may misjudge the distance between car C and your car.
Q0771 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What is the legal alcohol limit in micrograms per litre of breath if you are 20 or over?
  • [A] 400mcg/litre of breath
  • [B] 350mcg/litre of breath
  • [C] 250mcg/litre of breath ✔ Correct
  • [D] 100mcg/litre of breath
  • [E] E. Zero
Explanation: Correct. The maximum permissible level is 250mcg/litre of breath, although any amount of alcohol affects your reaction times so it is recommended you don't drink at all before driving.
Q0772 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When you are coming up to traffic signals and the signals change from green to yellow, what should you do?
  • [A] Drive faster to get through the lights
  • [B] Stop if it's safe to do so ✔ Correct
  • [C] Only stop if you are more than 15 metres from the intersection
Explanation: If it's safe to do so you should stop. This will vary according to the car's braking ability, current road conditions, and the ability for vehicles behind you to stop.
Q0773 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you do if you miss your exit on a motorway?
  • [A] Reverse all the way back to the exit by pulling into the hard shoulder
  • [B] Do a U-turn
  • [C] Exit at the next exit ✔ Correct
Explanation: Doing a U-turn would leave you facing oncoming traffic and reversing on the hard shoulder is dangerous.
Q0774 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you do if you see a pedestrian carrying a white cane across the street?
  • [A] Toot your horn to warn them that you are there and they need to hurry up
  • [B] Stop and wait for them to cross ✔ Correct
  • [C] Speed up and drive past them
Explanation: You should stop and let them cross as a white cane means that the person has impaired vision and may not be able to see your vehicle.
Q0775 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Where would you see this cat's eye?
  • [A] Left side of road
  • [B] Centre line of road ✔ Correct
  • [C] Right side of road
  • [D] Passing lane
Explanation: The centre line of the road is marked with white's cat's eyes.
Q0776 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
The safest way to drive up to intersections is what?
  • [A] Look right of you - you have to give way to the right
  • [B] Look left of you
  • [C] Look behind you
  • [D] Look in front of you
  • [E] E. All the above ✔ Correct
Explanation: At intersections, you should check all around you for other vehicles and you should be extra cautious.
Q0777 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What must you do when you come up to a school patrol crossing and both signs are held out?
  • [A] Stop until the signs are pulled back in ✔ Correct
  • [B] If the children aren't ready to cross then carry on
  • [C] Stop and wait for the children to cross
Explanation: Correct. Wait until the signs are back in as children can be unpredictable.
Q0778 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you do before crossing a railway level crossing? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Look right and left up the tracks ✔ Correct
  • [B] Check there's room for your vehicle on the other side of the crossing
  • [C] Ensure there are no barriers or red flashing lights
  • [D] Make sure there's a speed limit sign on the other side of the crossing
Explanation: A, B and C are the correct answers. First off, make sure there is no train coming, then make sure there is room on the crossing for your vehicle so you don't get stranded on the tracks.
Q0779 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When driving past a cyclist, what is the recommended distance you should allow?
  • [A] 1m
  • [B] 1.5m ✔ Correct
  • [C] 2m
  • [D] 2.5m
Explanation: Between your vehicle and a cyclist you must leave at least a 1.5m gap.
Q0780 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When there are farm animals coming towards you on the road, what should you do?
  • [A] Tap your brakes to warn any drivers behind you
  • [B] Slow down or pull over until the animals have moved past you ✔ Correct
  • [C] Toot your horn to scare the animals off the road
  • [D] Have your passenger get out and clear a path
Explanation: It's best to slow down or even stop until the animals pass, but be sure to follow any instructions the farmer gives you.
Q0781 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Which of these should you do if you're coming up to a railway level crossing? Check all that apply.
  • [A] It's safe to continue at your current speed if there are no barrier arms because that railway line isn't used
  • [B] Slow down and prepare to stop ✔ Correct
  • [C] Look both ways before proceeding
  • [D] If there's nothing blocking your path and no train coming then it is safe to cross
Explanation: You should be cautious when crossing to ensure that there is no train coming and that you can cross your whole vehicle to the other side. Just because there are no barriers doesn't mean the line isn't used.
Q0782 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you do when opening the car door if you look in the mirror and see a cyclist?
  • [A] Open the door slowly so the cyclist has time to react
  • [B] Cyclists always leave 1.5m gap between themselves and cars- open it as per normal
  • [C] Wait until the cyclist has passed ✔ Correct
  • [D] Sound your horn to warn the cyclist before you open your door
Explanation: The cyclist may not see you opening your door or may be forced into other traffic, always wait until the cyclist has passed.
Q0783 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What does this sign mean?
  • [A] The left side of a bridge ✔ Correct
  • [B] The right side of a bridge
  • [C] The left lane of a road
  • [D] The right lane of a road
Explanation: The left side of a bridge is indicated by this marker.
Q0784 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
You must NOT open the door of a motor vehicle when?
  • [A] If it's likely to hit someone or something, such as a cyclist ✔ Correct
  • [B] Anytime the car is moving
  • [C] When a police officer asks you to get out of the car
  • [D] A bus stop is within 10 metres of where you have parked
Explanation: When you are moving or stationary, a door can become an obstacle to a cyclist.
Q0785 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
This cat's eye would be found where?
  • [A] Right side of road
  • [B] Centre line of road ✔ Correct
  • [C] No passing lane
  • [D] Left side of road
Explanation: To the left of the centre line of the road is marked with white cat's eyes.
Q0786 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When driving under the influence of alcohol how does that in turn affect your driving?
  • [A] Your reactions can speed up
  • [B] It helps you make better judgement calls
  • [C] It slows down your reaction time ✔ Correct
  • [D] It increases your alertness
Explanation: Any amount of alcohol can slow down your reaction time and inhibit your driving.
Q0787 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What does a white diamond painted on the road mean?
  • [A] There is a sharp turn in the road
  • [B] You are approaching a school zone
  • [C] Your lane is ending
  • [D] You are approaching a pedestrian crossing ✔ Correct
Explanation: Most of pedestrian crossings will have a diamond painted on them although some will not.
Q0788 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When driving on a motorway what are you NOT permitted to do? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Make a U-turn ✔ Correct
  • [B] Stop (unless in an emergency or waiting in queued traffic)
  • [C] Drop off or pick-up passengers
  • [D] Pass a car on the left
Explanation: If it's safe to do so and there are two or more lanes on your side of the road then you can pass a car on the left.
Q0789 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What else are you advised to do when driving into bright sunlight besides using your sunglasses and your vehicle sun visors for safety? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Keep your windscreen clean ✔ Correct
  • [B] Turn your hazard lights on
  • [C] Slow down, or pull over until visibility improves
  • [D] Drive on the far right hand side of the road
Explanation: It's advised that you slow down and pull over until your eyes have adjusted to the light, and/or you should keep your windscreen clean.
Q0790 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
If you want to carry goods inside a car, what is the safest way?
  • [A] In the boot ✔ Correct
  • [B] On the front seat
  • [C] Have your passenger hold them
  • [D] On your lap
Explanation: Correct. Goods won't be loose in the cabin if you keep the goods in the boot. That way if you have to stop quickly the heavy items won't be propelled forward.
Q0791 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When MUST you dip your vehicle's headlights if you are driving at night with your high beams on? Check all that apply.
  • [A] You're driving in an area with street lights
  • [B] When traffic is being directed by a police officer ✔ Correct
  • [C] When you are following another car
  • [D] When another car is driving towards you
  • [E] E. If you stop on the side of the road
Explanation: When driving in an area with street lights you don't need to dip your lights, but for all the other circumstances listed you do.
Q0792 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you be aware of when you purchase a vehicle? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Unpaid loans that you will be liable to pay if they are not cleared before the car is transferred in your name ✔ Correct
  • [B] A stolen vehicle
  • [C] Suspicious odometer
  • [D] WoF and/or registration has expired
Explanation: Before you purchase a car you should get a vehicle history report.
Q0793 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
If you saw this cat's eye, where would you be?
  • [A] Right side of the road
  • [B] Centre line of road ✔ Correct
  • [C] No passing lane
  • [D] Parking lane
Explanation: The centre line of the road is marked with white cat's eyes.
Q0794 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When you're driving past a cyclist what is the recommended distance to leave between you and them?
  • [A] 3m
  • [B] 1.5m ✔ Correct
  • [C] 2m
  • [D] 2.5m
Explanation: You are required to leave 1.5m of space between your vehicle and a cyclist.
Q0795 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Can you drag a load you are carrying in your vehicle on the ground?
  • [A] No ✔ Correct
  • [B] Yes
Explanation: No, because it could break, come loose because of extra friction or it might get caught on the road.
Q0796 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What are you required to do when you are given medication by your doctor that does not affect your driving?
  • [A] Don't drive, you shouldn't be driving on any kind of medication
  • [B] You can drive whenever you want ✔ Correct
  • [C] You must notify the police where and when you are driving
Explanation: Nothing. You are free to drive as normal if the medication you are given doesn't affect your driving ability.
Q0797 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
While driving are you permitted to text (read, write, or send an SMS)?
  • [A] Yes - at any time
  • [B] Yes, with a hands-free phone kit
  • [C] No ✔ Correct
Explanation: No, you are not permitted to text while driving.
Q0798 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should your speed be when passing a bus displaying a School sign that has stopped to let children on or off?
  • [A] 20kph ✔ Correct
  • [B] 25kph
  • [C] 50kph
  • [D] 100kph
Explanation: Slow down to 20kph to reduce the chance of an accident as a child may dash out from in front of the bus.
Q0799 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
If the vehicle behind you starts to pass you, what should you do?
  • [A] Move over to the far left hand side of the road ✔ Correct
  • [B] Maintain your speed
  • [C] The left of the lane is more dangerous so remain in the middle of your lane
  • [D] Be prepared to slow down to ensure a safe passing manoeuvre
Explanation: Don't drive on the verge and stay on the road when moving to the left. Moving too far over can cause a tyre puncture as debris from road sweepers may be there. Remaining in the middle of your lane makes it more dangerous for other vehicles to pass. If the other driver misjudges...
Q0800 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Are you permitted to pass on the left like this?
  • [A] Yes ✔ Correct
  • [B] No
Explanation: You can pass on the left if there are two lanes on your side of the road and it's safe to do so.
Q0801 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What does this sign mean?
  • [A] The corner is at a 35 degree angle
  • [B] In 35 metres there is a sharp corner
  • [C] The recommended speed for this corner is 35kph ✔ Correct
Explanation: The number shows the maximum speed for safe travel around the corner and the chevrons show the direction of the corner.
Q0802 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When another vehicle is following too closely, what should you do?
  • [A] Make it easier for them to pass by moving to the left and slowing down ✔ Correct
  • [B] Driver faster so that you're not holding them up
  • [C] Tell them to drop back by pumping your brakes
  • [D] Turn your hazards on
Explanation: Correct. Let the vehicle pass if you are holding it up.
Q0803 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
You must signal for at least three seconds before making a lane change to your left. What else must you do? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Check your blind spots ✔ Correct
  • [B] Slow down
  • [C] Speed up
  • [D] Tap your brakes to warn the other drivers
Explanation: Correct. Be sure to turn your head to check your blind spot over your left shoulder.
Q0804 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What does this traffic signal mean?
  • [A] Stop if you can do so safely ✔ Correct
  • [B] Drive faster to get through the junction
Explanation: Correct. You must stop safely if you can.
Q0805 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What must you do before you move your vehicle out of a parking space into the traffic flow? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Signal for at least three seconds ✔ Correct
  • [B] Check your blind spots
  • [C] Wait for a space in the traffic
Explanation: When moving into traffic, all of these should be considered.
Q0806 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you do when you are following a vehicle on a gravel road? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Try and overtake the vehicle in front
  • [B] Drop back so you're not in the dust cloud ✔ Correct
  • [C] Put your full beam lights on so that other drivers pull over
  • [D] If visibility is reduced significantly put your low beams on
  • [E] E. Drive down the middle of the road
Explanation: You should slow down so that you're not blinded by the dust cloud and to lower your chance of a flying stone cracking your windscreen. Having your lights on will also help other drivers see you, particularly if you are covered by a dust cloud from the driver in front.
Q0807 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you do when following a vehicle on a gravel road? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Try and overtake the vehicle in front
  • [B] Drop back so you're not in the dust cloud ✔ Correct
  • [C] Put your full beam lights on so that other drivers pull over
  • [D] If visibility is reduced significantly put your low beams on
  • [E] E. Drive down the middle of the road
Explanation: You should slow down so that you're not blinded by the dust cloud and to lower your chance of a flying stone cracking your windscreen. Having your lights on will also help other drivers see you, particularly if you are covered by a dust cloud from the driver in front.
Q0808 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
You should use sunglasses and your vehicle sun visors for safety when driving into bright sunlight. What else is advised? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Keep your windscreen clean ✔ Correct
  • [B] Turn your lights off
  • [C] Slow down, or pull over until visibility improves
  • [D] Keep your eyes focused on the centre of the road
Explanation: You can slow down or pull over until your eyes have adjusted to the light and you should keep your windscreen clean.
Q0809 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
If you are carrying a load, can it drag on the ground?
  • [A] No ✔ Correct
  • [B] Yes
Explanation: Correct. It could break or get caught on the road and come loose because of the extra friction.
Q0810 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
You must signal for at least three seconds before making a lane change to your left, what else must you do? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Check your blind spots ✔ Correct
  • [B] Slow down
  • [C] Speed up
  • [D] Tap your brakes to warn the other drivers
Explanation: Correct. Be sure to check your blind spot over your left shoulder.
Q0811 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What must you do when you are coming up to a one-way bridge and you see this sign?
  • [A] If there is no traffic approaching then cross the bridge
  • [B] If you see traffic coming towards you stop and wait until it's clear before you cross the bridge ✔ Correct
  • [C] You have the right of way across the bridge, you can keep going
Explanation: You must stop to let the traffic coming towards you through, as they have the right of way. However, you don't need to stop if there is nothing coming, unless there is a stop sign.
Q0812 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What do these mean?
  • [A] Taxis, buses, and bikes cannot park here
  • [B] When the light is lit, buses, trams, and bikes can ignore the red traffic signal and pass through ✔ Correct
  • [C] This is a lane only for bikes, trams and buses
  • [D] Buses, trams and bikes must wait to proceed before other traffic has passed when the light is lit
Explanation: Trams, buses, or bicycles are allowed to go through a red light before it turns green for all other traffic.
Q0813 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What does this traffic signal mean?
  • [A] Stop if you can do so safely ✔ Correct
  • [B] Drive faster to get through the junction
Explanation: Correct. You must stop safely if you can.
Q0814 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
This traffic signal means?
  • [A] If you can do so safely then you must stop ✔ Correct
  • [B] Speed up to get through the junction
Explanation: It means that you must stop safely if you are able to do so.
Q0815 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should your speed be when passing a bus that has stopped to let children on or off and is showing a School sign?
  • [A] 20kph ✔ Correct
  • [B] 50kph
  • [C] 70kph
  • [D] 100kph
Explanation: Correct. Slow down to 20kph as a child may run out in front of the bus.
Q0816 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What does T2 mean on a Transit Lane sign?
  • [A] After 2am this lane can be used
  • [B] Only two passenger vehicles can use this lane
  • [C] Only vehicles with less than two people inside can use this lane
  • [D] Only vehicles carrying two or more people can use this lane ✔ Correct
  • [E] E. This lane is for buses and taxis only
Explanation: Motorcycles, cycles, passenger service vehicles, and vehicles carrying at least two people can use this transit lane.
Q0817 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What does this sign mean?
  • [A] 35 kph until the next town
  • [B] A corner in 35 metres
  • [C] The recommended speed for this corner is 35kph ✔ Correct
Explanation: The number shows the recommended safe maximum speed for travelling around a corner and the chevrons show the direction of the corner.
Q0818 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When you have this traffic signal, can you turn left?
  • [A] Yes
  • [B] No ✔ Correct
Explanation: Only vehicles that are turning right can go. A red light is for traffic turning let and traffic driving straight through.
Q0819 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What do you have to do if you are given medication by your doctor that does not affect your driving?
  • [A] You shouldn't be driving on any medication- do not drive
  • [B] You can drive whenever you want ✔ Correct
  • [C] You must report to at least 3 people where you are driving at all times
Explanation: You are free to drive as normal if the medication does not impact your driving ability.
Q0820 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you do when passing a horse and rider?
  • [A] Toot your horn to warn them that you are behind them
  • [B] Speed by the horse to avoid hitting it
  • [C] Pass slowly ✔ Correct
  • [D] Flash your high beams to warn them you are there
Explanation: Slow down and prepare to stop as horses can be easily frightened. Overtake gently, without revving the engine.
Q0821 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you do if there are farm animals coming towards you on the road?
  • [A] The animals will move out of the way if you flash your lights
  • [B] Slow down and pull over until the animals have past you. ✔ Correct
  • [C] Get out of the car and help the farmer move the animals
  • [D] Have the passenger in the car get out and clear a path through the animals
Explanation: Slow down or even stop until the animals have past you. However, you should listen to any instructions the farmer gives you.
Q0822 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you do when a flock of sheep are coming toward you on a country road? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Toot your horn and continue driving, they will get out of the way
  • [B] Slow down and be prepared to stop ✔ Correct
  • [C] Follow the farmer's instructions
  • [D] Drive slowly and turn on your high beam lights
Explanation: Slow down and follow any instructions the farmer gives you and don't toot your horn as it may frighten them.
Q0823 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Which hazard out of the four marked is most likely to require you to take urgent action? (You are the driver of the blue car).
  • [A] The car that is parked
  • [B] The car that is reversing ✔ Correct
  • [C] The car coming towards you
  • [D] The car parked on the opposite side of the road
Explanation: The main hazard is the reversing car. You should be prepared to stop if necessary as you may be in the car's blind spot.
Q0824 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When MUST you dip your vehicle's headlights if you are driving at night with your high beams on? Check all that apply.
  • [A] You're driving in an area with street lights
  • [B] When traffic is being directed by a police officer ✔ Correct
  • [C] When you are following another car
  • [D] When another car is driving towards you
  • [E] E. If you stop on the side of the road
Explanation: When driving in an area with street lights, you don't need to dip your lights, but for all the other circumstances listed you do.
Q0825 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
If another vehicle is following you closely, what should you do?
  • [A] Make it easier for them to pass by moving to the left and slowing down ✔ Correct
  • [B] Speed up quickly so that you're no longer holding them up
  • [C] Tell them to fall back by pumping your brakes a few times
  • [D] Put your lights on high beam
Explanation: Correct. You must let the vehicle pass if you are holding it up.
Q0826 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Are you permitted to pass on a solid yellow line?
  • [A] No
  • [B] Yes
  • [C] If you can make the pass without crossing the yellow line and can see 100m in front of you for the whole time you are passing then you can pass ✔ Correct
Explanation: As long as you stay to the left of the yellow line in this situation then you can pass a car.
Q0827 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
If the vehicle behind you wishes to pass what should you do?
  • [A] Speed up and drive past them
  • [B] Pull to the left to let them pass ✔ Correct
  • [C] Nothing- it is their responsibility to overtake safely
  • [D] Speed up and signal right
Explanation: You should allow the other driver to pass when it's safe out of common courtesy and respect.
Q0828 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When you have this traffic signal can you turn right?
  • [A] No, there's a blue arrow
  • [B] No, you can only drive straight through
  • [C] Yes, but only if there are no vehicles coming. ✔ Correct
Explanation: Yes, but you must ensure it is safe and that there are no vehicles coming straight through the intersection.
Q0829 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Of the four hazards marked, which one is most likely to require you to take urgent action if you are the driver of the blue car?
  • [A] The person hitching a lift (A)
  • [B] The child on the side of the road (B) ✔ Correct
  • [C] The parked car (C)
  • [D] The parked car that is partially obscured from your view (D)
Explanation: This child's attention is on the child on the side of the road. As you can see children are very unpredictable around roads.
Q0830 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When you are approaching traffic signals and the signals change from green to yellow, what should you do?
  • [A] Drive faster to get through the lights
  • [B] Stop if it's safe to do so ✔ Correct
  • [C] Stop if you are more than 20 metres from the intersection
Explanation: If it's safe to do so you should stop, this will vary according to the car's braking ability, current road conditions, and the ability for vehicles behind you to stop.
Q0831 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Of the four hazards marked, which one is most likely to require you to take urgent action as the driver of the blue car?
  • [A] The cyclist ✔ Correct
  • [B] The parked car on your side of the road
  • [C] The car coming at you
  • [D] The pedestrian on the opposite footpath
Explanation: Correct. The cyclist may turn in front of you.
Q0832 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you be aware of when you purchase a vehicle? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Unpaid loans that you will be liable to pay if they are not cleared before the car is transferred in your name ✔ Correct
  • [B] A stolen vehicle
  • [C] Suspicious odometer
  • [D] WoF and/or registration has expired
Explanation: Before you purchase a car you should get a vehicle history report.
Q0833 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Which of the four hazards is most likely going to require you, the driver of blue car, to take urgent action?
  • [A] The cyclist ✔ Correct
  • [B] The parked vehicle on your side of the road
  • [C] The vehicle coming towards you
  • [D] The pedestrian on the opposite footpath
Explanation: The cyclist may turn in front of you, as they are already on the road.
Q0834 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
GVM stands for?
  • [A] Generic Vehicle Maintenance
  • [B] Gross Vehicle Mass ✔ Correct
  • [C] General Vehicle Make
Explanation: GVM stands for Gross Vehicle Mass, or how heavy the vehicle is.
Q0835 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you do if you see a pedestrian carrying a white cane across the street?
  • [A] Toot your horn to warn them that you are there and they need to hurry up
  • [B] Stop and wait for them to cross ✔ Correct
  • [C] Speed up and drive past them
Explanation: You should stop and let them cross as a white cane means that the person has impaired vision and may not be able to see your vehicle.
Q0836 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you do if you miss your exit on a motorway?
  • [A] Reverse back to the last exit by pulling into the hard shoulder
  • [B] Do a U-turn
  • [C] Exit at the next exit ✔ Correct
Explanation: Doing a U-turn would leave you facing oncoming traffic and reversing on the hard shoulder; this is dangerous.
Q0837 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
If you want to carry goods inside a car what is the safest way?
  • [A] In the boot ✔ Correct
  • [B] On the front seat
  • [C] Have your passenger hold them
  • [D] On your lap
Explanation: Correct. Goods won't be loose in the cabin if you keep the goods in the boot. That way if you have to stop quickly the heavy items won't be propelled forward.
Q0838 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you do if you are driving in a funeral procession?
  • [A] Keep your headlights on dip ✔ Correct
  • [B] Turn your hazard lights on
  • [C] Toot your horn
  • [D] Drive with the driver's window down
Explanation: To let other cars know that you're part of a funeral procession, keep your headlights dipped.
Q0839 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Alcohol affects your driving in what way?
  • [A] It speeds up your reaction time
  • [B] It makes you a better judge of distance
  • [C] It slows your reaction time ✔ Correct
  • [D] It provides you with more focus
Explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol can affect your driving ability and slow your reactions.
Q0840 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
The open road speed limit for a car or motorbike is what?
  • [A] 100kph ✔ Correct
  • [B] 110kph
  • [C] 80kph
  • [D] 70kph
Explanation: The maximum speed that you are allowed to drive on the open road is 100kph.
Q0841 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
You see this sign when you are coming up to a one-lane bridge. What must you do?
  • [A] Stop and cross the bridge if there is no traffic coming
  • [B] If there is traffic coming towards you across the bridge then stop and wait until it's clear ✔ Correct
  • [C] You have right of way across the bridge- continue on
Explanation: This sign means that you must stop to let the traffic coming towards you through, as they have the right of way. If there's nothing coming and you don't see a stop sign then you don't have to stop.
Q0842 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What does this sign mean?
  • [A] The left side of a bridge ✔ Correct
  • [B] The right side of a bridge
  • [C] The left side of a road
  • [D] The right side of a road
Explanation: Correct. This sign identifies the left side of a bridge.
Q0843 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Which of these should you do if you're coming up to a railway level crossing? Check all that apply.
  • [A] The railway line isn't being used so it's safe to continue at the speed you're travelling as long as there are no barrier arms
  • [B] Slow down and get ready to stop ✔ Correct
  • [C] Before you cross make sure you've checked both ways
  • [D] If there are no trains coming and nothing blocking your path then you can cross
Explanation: You should be cautious when crossing to ensure that there is no train coming and that you can cross your whole vehicle to the other side. Just because there are no barriers doesn't mean the line isn't used.
Q0844 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Before reversing your vehicle, how would you check for hazards? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Check you wing mirrors and rear-view mirror ✔ Correct
  • [B] Look over your shoulder
  • [C] Get out and walk around the vehicle
  • [D] If your vehicle has reversing sensors or cameras, make sure that they are activated
Explanation: These are all valid ways to check for hazards before reversing.
Q0845 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What does oversteer mean?
  • [A] When you hit the verge on the inside of the a corner because you turned too sharply
  • [B] When you cross onto the wrong side of the road because you misjudged turning right into an intersection
  • [C] When the back wheels of the car start skidding the opposite way to which you are turning ✔ Correct
Explanation: When you turn too sharply, this can cause the rear wheels to start skidding, and this is what oversteer is.
Q0846 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you do when a flock of sheep are coming towards you on a country road? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Toot your horn and continue driving, they will get out of the way
  • [B] Slow down and be prepared to stop ✔ Correct
  • [C] Follow the farmer's instructions
  • [D] Drive slowly and turn on your high beam lights
Explanation: Slow down and follow any instructions the farmer gives you and don't toot your horn as it may frighten them.
Q0847 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
After ensuring that it's safe to move out from the kerb into the traffic flow, how long should you indicate for?
  • [A] 1 second
  • [B] 2 seconds
  • [C] 3 seconds ✔ Correct
  • [D] 4 seconds
Explanation: A safe time to signal for is three seconds.
Q0848 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What does this sign mean?
  • [A] Bridge
  • [B] Roundabout ✔ Correct
  • [C] Tunnel
Explanation: This sign indicates that you should be preparing to give way as you are coming up to a roundabout.
