  • [D] Continue driving slowly with your hazard lights on
  • [E] E. Continue driving with your interior lights on
Explanation: If your lights are out, you will not be visible to other drivers; never park on the right facing traffic.
Q0996 All Classes Emergencies Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
If glass falls on the road from your vehicle, what must you do? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Nothing is required
  • [B] If it can be done quickly and safely then stop and remove the glass yourself ✔ Correct
  • [C] If you are physically not able to pick it up then tell the police
Explanation: If you can't remove glass from the road yourself then you must report it.
Q0997 All Classes Emergencies Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
If you have a rear tyre blowout, what could happen?
  • [A] The back end will sway away from the side of the blowout
  • [B] The back end could sway towards the blow out
  • [C] The front end will pull side to side
  • [D] The front may pull to the other side of the blowout
  • [E] E. The back end will move from side to side ✔ Correct
Explanation: It is likely that the back end will swing out first on the same side as the blowout and it will sway from side to side.
Q0998 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Emergencies Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
If an ambulance comes up behind you with flashing red lights and it's siren on, what should you do?
  • [A] Come to a stop as fast as possible
  • [B] The ambulance driver will find a way to get by you, keep driving at the same speed
  • [C] Drive as fast as you can safely so that you're not holding the ambulance up
  • [D] Slow down or stop if necessary and pull over to the left ✔ Correct
Explanation: Do everything you can to let the ambulance pass you. Slowing down shortens the time it takes to overtake you and pulling to the left gives the ambulance more room.
Q0999 All Classes Emergencies Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you do if you are driving past a line of parked cars and you notice a ball bouncing out into the road ahead?
  • [A] It doesn't matter if it hits the car, just keep driving on your side of the road
  • [B] Keep on your side of the road and stop safely ✔ Correct
  • [C] Try to avoid the ball by immediately swerving to the side of the road
  • [D] Flash your headlights
Explanation: Swerving to the other side of the road can create a hazard while hitting the ball might send it into the path of another vehicle.
Q1000 All Classes Emergencies Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
You had a crash and you are the driver, who must you report the crash to?
  • [A] A fire officer
  • [B] A police officer ✔ Correct
  • [C] The next of kin of the person you injured
  • [D] A judge
  • [E] E. Somebody who works at the court
Explanation: Within 24 hours you must report the crash to a police officer.
Q1001 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Emergencies Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
If glass falls on the road from your vehicle, what must you do? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Nothing is required
  • [B] If it can be done quickly and safely then stop and remove the glass yourself ✔ Correct
  • [C] If you are physically not able to pick it up then tell the police
Explanation: If you can't remove glass from the road yourself, then you must report it.
Q1002 Class 1 (Car) Car - Emergencies DT Driver Training (Extended)
If you are a driver involved in a crash, what is the FIRST action you should take?
  • [A] Call the police
  • [B] Stop and check to see if anyone is hurt ✔ Correct
  • [C] Call for an ambulance
  • [D] Leave the scene to tell someone
  • [E] Call a family member or friend
Explanation: First actions after a car crash If you are involved in a crash and not badly hurt, the first thing to do is check for other people's injuries. Then see if your vehicle can be moved out of danger once you have checked on other vehicle occupants and called emergency services....
Q1003 Class 1 (Car) Car - Emergencies DT Driver Training (Extended)
If you are the driver and you hurt somebody in a crash, who must you report it to?
  • [A] An ambulance officer
  • [B] A police officer ✔ Correct
  • [C] The next of kin of the person you injured
  • [D] A lawyer
  • [E] A clerk of the court
Explanation: The process after a car crash with injuries If you have a crash your first priority is to check whether other people need medical assistance - check airways, breathing and circulation - and you must report it to a police officer within 24 hours. Call 111 for an ambulance if...
Q1004 Class 1 (Car) Car - Emergencies DT Driver Training (Extended)
Who can put a crash or accident sign out?
  • [A] An ambulance officer
  • [B] A police officer ✔ Correct
  • [C] A council officer
  • [D] A member of the public
Explanation: Who can place an Accident or Crash sign on the road? Only a police officer can place an accident sign on the road. Other road users can place a warning triangle on the road to inform people that there's an accident. If there is an accident sign it could be that there is debris...
Q1005 Class 1 (Car) Car - Emergencies DT Driver Training (Extended)
The bonnet of your vehicle lifts up while you are driving and you cannot see. What should you do? Select all that apply.
  • [A] Brake suddenly so you don't leave the road
  • [B] Look through the gap underneath the bonnet or out of the side window
  • [C] Signal, brake smoothly, and pull to the side of the road, then refasten the bonnet ✔ Correct
  • [D] Turn on your headlights and look out of the side window
Explanation: What happens if your bonnet latch fails? It's extremely unlikely that your bonnet latch or catch will fail. Almost all bonnet catches have a two-stage release so that if the first stage fails it catches on the second stage. However, it's not unheard of as you can see in this...
Q1006 Class 1 (Car) Car - Emergencies DT Driver Training (Extended)
What should you do if an ambulance comes up behind you flashing red lights or sounding its siren?
  • [A] Stop quickly
  • [B] Maintain your speed - the ambulance driver will find a way around you
  • [C] Speed up so that you don't hold the ambulance up
  • [D] Pull over to the left and slow down or stop if necessary ✔ Correct
Explanation: When you hear a siren or see red flashing lights from an ambulance or fire engine, if they are following you, you must slow down and pull over. Stop if necessary. If a police car is following you with its lights flashing (which will be red and blue), then you must stop unless it...
Q1007 Class 1 (Car) Car - Emergencies DT Driver Training (Extended)
Which one of the following is most likely to cause an emergency situation?
  • [A] Practicing skids on a quiet road ✔ Correct
  • [B] Towing a trailer
  • [C] Driving defensively
  • [D] Not using your full beam headlights when driving in rural areas at night
Explanation: Reckless driving Reckless driving is driving without consideration for other road users or yourself . A number of driving practices can be considered reckless driving: Road rage Inappropriate speed Driving after drinking or taking drugs Dangerous overtaking Not paying attention...
Motorcycle Specific (Class 6) 142 Questions
Q1008 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Engine seizure is usually imminient when:
  • [A] Loss of power and a change in the sound ✔ Correct
  • [B] More power
  • [C] Shrieks and pops coming from the exhaust
  • [D] Blue and red smoke emerging from the unit
Explanation: Correct. The power drops and there may be a change in the engine tone, as well when an engine is about to seize.
Q1009 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What is it best to do before going through a right hand curve?
  • [A] Move to the left hand side of the road
  • [B] Move to the right hand side of the road
  • [C] Slow down ✔ Correct
Explanation: Slowing down is the best plan, as new motorcycle riders often enter turns too quickly. They tend to cross into another lane of traffic or go off the road because they can't hold the turn, or they brake too hard and skid out of control.
Q1010 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Would a motorbike fail its warrant of fitness if it only had one indicator working?
  • [A] No, it wouldn't fail because the rider can still use hand signals
  • [B] Yes ✔ Correct
Explanation: Although you could use hand signals, your bike would fail its warrant of fitness if you only had one indicator light working.
Q1011 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you do if you get a blowout or puncture on your motorcycle? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Bring the bike to a quick stop by braking hard
  • [B] Let the motorbike slow down without braking by gradually closing the throttle ✔ Correct
  • [C] If the front wheel goes flat shift your weight as far back as possible
  • [D] If the back tyre goes flat just sit normally
Explanation: If possible, avoid braking and close the throttle gradually, letting the bike slowly stop. Signal and move to the side of the road and if your back tyre deflates keep your weight neutral. If your front tyre deflates move your weight to the back.
Q1012 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
If an oncoming vehicle seems ready to cross your path, what should you do?
  • [A] Speed up and move to the right side of your lane
  • [B] Speed up and move to the left side in your lane
  • [C] Slow down and move to the right hand side of your lane
  • [D] Slow down and move to the left hand side in your lane ✔ Correct
Explanation: Move to the left hand side of your lane and slow down. If there are stationary vehicles blocking the driver's view then take extra caution and sound your horn if necessary.
Q1013 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Check all those that apply as to why face protection is important when on a motorcycle?
  • [A] It protects the rider's identity as other road users won't be able to distinguish who the rider is
  • [B] The rider's eyes and face are protected from wind, rain, insects, dust and other debris ✔ Correct
  • [C] It keeps the face of the rider warm in cooler temperatures
  • [D] It's impossible to breath without one above 80kph
Explanation: To learn more, read about motorbike protective clothing here: (copy and paste it) http://www.nzta.govt.nz/resources/roadcode/motorcycle-road-code/you-and-your-motorcycle/wearing-the-right-gear.html
Q1014 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
In a line of stopped or moving traffic, what should you do?
  • [A] Drive on the right past the traffic
  • [B] Drive on the left past the traffic
  • [C] Stay in the centre of your lane ✔ Correct
  • [D] Stay in the right hand side of your lane
  • [E] E. Stay in the left hand side of your lane
Explanation: Be as visible as possible by staying in the middle of your lane and protect your lane position from other vehicles. Avoid squeezing by other traffic to reduce your risk of an accident.
Q1015 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
If you become sleepy while driving what should you do? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Open the window
  • [B] Pull over as soon as possible to a safe place ✔ Correct
  • [C] Get off your bike if you're on a motorbike or take a short nap (15-20 minutes) in the passenger seat if you are driving
  • [D] After you've woken up wait for 10 minutes until you start driving again
  • [E] E. Pull over and grab a coffee to help wake yourself up
Explanation: This dramatically increases your chances of having an accident so you need to pull over, take a nap, then wait for 10 minutes to ensure that you are awake. Once you start to feel this way, your reactions slow and you will soon start to take micro sleeps where you close your eyes...
Q1016 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What might be likely to happen on a high-crowned road, and in what situation should you reduce speed?
  • [A] You could lose control because your front wheel may leave the road surface
  • [B] You could lose control because your rear wheel could leave the road surface
  • [C] There may be another vehicle on your side of the road as you come over the crest
  • [D] Your right peg might hit the road as you turn right ✔ Correct
Explanation: There will be less clearance between your right peg and the road as you turn right if the road has a high centre. The turn will also be more difficult due to the downslope.
Q1017 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you do if you see a vehicle ahead of you about to do a U-turn or pull out of a parking space?
  • [A] Speed up and move right in your lane
  • [B] Speed up and move left in your lane
  • [C] Slow down and move to the right hand side of your lane ✔ Correct
  • [D] Slow down and move to the left hand side in your lane
Explanation: To give the other driver more time to react, slow down and move to the right of the lane.
Q1018 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What must you clean your helmet with if it gets dirty?
  • [A] A mild cleaner
  • [B] Bleach
  • [C] Soap and water ✔ Correct
Explanation: Only use soap and water, as other solvents and cleaning solutions can weaken the shell.
Q1019 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When driving at night, how can you get a better view of a road? Check those answers that apply.
  • [A] If another vehicle is approaching towards you, it is important to use your high beam light ✔ Correct
  • [B] Sit upright
  • [C] Use your car visor or sunglasses to cut-down on the glare
  • [D] Use another vehicle's tail lights to help judge the road ahead
Explanation: It is a good idea to use other vehicle's tail lights to help guide you to corners and bumps in the road. Be sure to sit upright and use your high beams (but not when in fog, following another vehicle, and when other vehicles are coming towards you).
Q1020 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
If you don't turn off your indicator, what is the danger?
  • [A] It will irritate other drivers which could cause road rage
  • [B] Other drivers may pull into your path, thinking you'll turn ✔ Correct
  • [C] Other drivers may think you're going straight and may turn in front of you
Explanation: Drivers may pull out in front of you because they will think that you are turning
Q1021 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you do if your helmet is falling apart?
  • [A] Repair the helmet with duct tape and superglue
  • [B] Throw it away and buy a new one ✔ Correct
  • [C] It's still safe to use if there are no cracks
  • [D] Sell it and buy a new one
Explanation: Even if there is no visible cracks, you should throw out the helmet and purchase a new one. There may be microscopic cracks that can weaken the helmet.
Q1022 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What is the maximum speed you can ride when towing, if your trailer including its load is up to half the weight of your motorbike?
  • [A] 45kph
  • [B] 60kph
  • [C] 80kph
  • [D] 90kph ✔ Correct
Explanation: 90kph is the maximum speed you are allowed to travel on the open road if your trailer is less than half the weight of your bike.
Q1023 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
In order for a motorcycle to carry a passenger which equipment must they have? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Foot pegs for both the driver and passenger ✔ Correct
  • [B] Enough room on the seat for two people without crowding
  • [C] The passenger requires a lap belt
  • [D] A 200cc engine at least
Explanation: You must have enough room on the seat for the driver to sit normally and the passenger to sit safety without hanging over the end of the seat. You must also have foot pegs for the passenger.
Q1024 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Motorcyclists can suffer from Hypothermia. What could cause this?
  • [A] Not enough clothing
  • [B] Dehydration
  • [C] Lack of food
  • [D] Wind ✔ Correct
Explanation: Your core body temperatures drop dangerously low with Hypothermia, reducing your reflexes. It can be deceptive as even on a nice day hypothermia can occur due to the wind chill.
Q1025 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
A learner motorcyclist is on an open road, what is the maximum speed?
  • [A] 50kph
  • [B] 60kph
  • [C] 80kph
  • [D] 100kph ✔ Correct
Explanation: Since Oct. 1 2011, a learner motorcyclist can drive on open road at a maximum of 100kph.
Q1026 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Check all of the scenarios that would make it easy to skid?
  • [A] Slightly over-inflated tyres ✔ Correct
  • [B] Slightly under-inflated tyres
  • [C] Braking too hard
  • [D] A shaded corner during winter
  • [E] E. Changing direction quickly
Explanation: Applying the brakes hard can cause a skid along with changing direction quickly. Under-inflated tyres cause more tyre surface to contact the road. Over-inflated tyres cause less tyre surface to be in contact with the road. A shaded corner in winter may have ice or snow.
Q1027 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What can you do to avoid skidding on slippery surfaces? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Only use the back brake, there's less risk of skidding because it's less powerful
  • [B] Ride at reduced speed, especially around corners ✔ Correct
  • [C] Brake earlier than usual and allow more time
  • [D] Use the front brake first
  • [E] E. There's more tyre contact in the corners so you should brake there
Explanation: Only brake when upright as braking in the corners adds extra force on the tyres. Don't use the back brake on its own, use the front brake gently to avoid locking it up and then use the back brake.
Q1028 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What position should your motorcycle be in when in an emergency braking situation?
  • [A] Turn hard to the right or left to keep away from danger
  • [B] Upright ✔ Correct
Explanation: The less grip you have if your motorbike is leaning, so upright is safest.
Q1029 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What's the maximum distance (either side of the centre line) that your load can extend when carrying a load on your motorbike?
  • [A] The maximum distance is 50cm from the centre line of the motorcycle ✔ Correct
  • [B] The maximum distance is 75cm from the centre line of the motorcycle.
  • [C] The maximum distance is 125cm from the centre line of the motorcycle.
  • [D] The maximum distance is 175cm from the centre line of the motorcycle.
Explanation: Correct. No more than 50cm either side of the centre line of your motorcycle.
Q1030 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When carrying a passenger on a motorcycle, what changes should you make to your motorcycle and riding style? Check all that apply.
  • [A] For a more comfortable ride, deflate the tyres slightly so that more tyre contacts the road
  • [B] To compensate for the change in angle of the motorcycle because of the passenger adjust the mirror and headlight ✔ Correct
  • [C] Adjust your shock absorbers (if possible) to be firmer
  • [D] Seat further up in your seat than you normally would
Explanation: You should put more air in your tyres, adjust your mirror and headlights and firm up your shock absorbers. Ride in your normal position and don't move forwards.
Q1031 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When riding on bitumen after a rain, what is the main danger?
  • [A] Glare from the sun
  • [B] Road markings and manhole covers ✔ Correct
  • [C] Wet bitumen is very slippery
  • [D] Other vehicles
Explanation: Metal manhole covers and painted lines are far more slippery when wet than bitumen is. You should also be cautious of the glare from the sun when the road is wet, this could make it difficult to see pedestrians, animals or potholes.
Q1032 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Why is it dangerous to travel in other riders' blind spots?
  • [A] It's not dangerous-the blind spot will change as soon as the rider starts to move and they’ll be able to see you
  • [B] The other motorist is more likely to move into your space, risking an accident ✔ Correct
Explanation: Blind spots can be really dangerous so you must drive defensively and anticipate where other's blind spots are.
Q1033 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What's the maximum distance in front and behind that your load can extend when carrying a load on your motorcycle?
  • [A] 1m each way ✔ Correct
  • [B] 1.5m each way
  • [C] 2m each way
Explanation: Correct. 1m in front of or behind your bike is what the load must not extend.
Q1034 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
The main reason for wearing protective clothing is what?
  • [A] Makes for a smoother ride
  • [B] To help prevent serious injury or death ✔ Correct
  • [C] To help other drivers see you better
Explanation: In an accident, protective clothing can increase your chance of survival.
Q1035 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you do if you are riding behind a large truck?
  • [A] Take advantage of the slipstreaming effect to save on fuel mileage by staying fairly close
  • [B] Stay in the middle of the road and ride fairly far back
  • [C] Ride on either the left or right so that you can see the vehicle's side mirror and stay fairly far back ✔ Correct
Explanation: The driver can see you if you stay back and ensure you can see the truck's side mirrors.
Q1036 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
An oncoming heavy vehicle has what effect?
  • [A] Nothing- compared to a car the frontal area of a bike is small
  • [B] Initially the wind will push you back, then suck you towards the vehicle ✔ Correct
  • [C] Initially the wind will suck you towards the vehicle, then push you back
Explanation: The slipstream behind the vehicle will suck you towards it and the pressure at the front of the vehicle will push you away.
Q1037 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When riding on slippery surfaces, what should you do? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Brake hard
  • [B] Use the front brake first ✔ Correct
  • [C] Ride slower
  • [D] So your tyre is in contact with the road, lean the bike over
  • [E] E. Stay in a high gear
Explanation: Only brake when you are upright and stay in a higher gear to avoid wheel spin. You should minimise turning, acceleration and braking as riding on slippery surfaces is dangerous.
Q1038 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
You are about to stop at a red light, it's raining and you notice that there is a large area that looks like an oil spillage. In order to stop safely, what should you do? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Stay upright ✔ Correct
  • [B] If it's safe to do so, ride through the stop light
  • [C] Apply the front brake first, but use both brakes
  • [D] Apply the rear brake first, but use both brakes
  • [E] E. Try to turn away from the oil if possible, don't try to steer if you're on the oil and don't make any sudden movements.
Explanation: The best chance of stopping without the bike skidding from underneath you is by staying upright and by being prepared to put your feet out if it allows you to balance better. This will also prop you up if the bike does slip, but keep in mind that if you take your foot off you...
Q1039 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Where would you be if the driver of a vehicle right in front of you cannot see you in either the rear view mirrors or by turning their head?
  • [A] Blind spot ✔ Correct
  • [B] Behind them
  • [C] Split second spot
Explanation: Correct. You must anticipate where other's blind spots are and drive defensively as blind spots can be really dangerous.
Q1040 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
It is best to place the beginner driver where when riding in groups?
  • [A] Front ✔ Correct
  • [B] Middle
  • [C] Back
  • [D] On the opposite side of the road
Explanation: Correct. In the front is best, as more experienced riders can keep an eye on them.
Q1041 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
If you need to slow in a curve, how should you do it?
  • [A] Use both brakes gently ✔ Correct
  • [B] Only use the front brake gently
  • [C] Only use the rear brake gently
Explanation: Correct. Always brake on the straight before it's too late, brake gently and try to avoid having to slow in a curve all together. Note that in this situation some motorcycle instructors advise you to only use the rear brake, which contradicts NZTA's information on this question.
Q1042 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Cross winds can occur when?
  • [A] When it's bad weather out
  • [B] As a large truck approaches you
  • [C] As you leave the protection of a building ✔ Correct
Explanation: Buildings can shelter your from cross winds, so when you emerge from a building your balance can be thrown off if you're suddenly be hit by a crosswind.
Q1043 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
How often does your motorcycle require a Warrant of Fitness inspection if your motorcycle was first registered before the 1st of January 2000?
  • [A] 12 months
  • [B] 6 months ✔ Correct
  • [C] 2 years
  • [D] 1.5 years
Explanation: You will need to take it for a WoF every six months if your bike was first registered before 1 January 2000.
Q1044 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When riding during the day what should you wear to help yourself be seen? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Wear high visibility clothing ✔ Correct
  • [B] Ride with your headlights on low beam
  • [C] Avoid other driver's blind spots by adjusting your riding position
  • [D] Use your horn to warn drivers
Explanation: You can wear high visibility clothing and your headlight must be on dip during the day. You can use your horn to warn other drivers but adjust your position in the road to anticipate where other vehicles' blind spots are, and avoid them.
Q1045 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Is the following statement true or false? Motorcycles do not have blind spots.
  • [A] TRUE
  • [B] FALSE ✔ Correct
Explanation: The spots the motorcycle rider can't see in the mirrors are called blind spots.
Q1046 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
How often does your motorcycle require a warrant of fitness inspection if it is more than three years old and was first registered in New Zealand or overseas on/after the 1st of January 2000?
  • [A] 12 months ✔ Correct
  • [B] 18 months
  • [C] 6 months
  • [D] 24 months
Explanation: Correct. Every 12 months a WoF inspection is required for all light vehicles first registered on or after 1 January 2000. However, brand new vehicles only require a WoF every three years after the initial inspection at time of purchase.
Q1047 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What must your motorcycle have in order to drive on the road legally and safely? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Current WoF ✔ Correct
  • [B] Two working headlights
  • [C] A horn that works
  • [D] A red reflector at the front
  • [E] E. A working speedometer
Explanation: To drive your bike legally and safely, you must have a current warrant of fitness, which means that you will need a red reflector on the back and a working horn and speedometer, as well as mudguards and several other requirements.
Q1048 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When riding a motorcycle, what is the best kind of footwear to wear?
  • [A] Running shoes because their grips can hold on to the pegs better
  • [B] Golf shoes because of their spikes
  • [C] Boots that cover your ankles ✔ Correct
Explanation: Boots provide the best protection, so they are your best option.
Q1049 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Motorcycle crashes at intersections are mostly caused from?
  • [A] Loss of control from front wheels skidding
  • [B] Loss of control from rear wheels skidding
  • [C] Vehicle pulling into the motorbike's path ✔ Correct
  • [D] Driver fatigue
Explanation: Pulling out from a side street or a vehicle making a turn across a motorcycle's path are the most common causes of motorbike crashes.
Q1050 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Where should your feet be when seated on your motorcycle?
  • [A] On the pillion foot rests
  • [B] Firm on the foot rests ✔ Correct
  • [C] Away from the controls
  • [D] Tilted away from the front
Explanation: The feet should be near the controls with the feet firmly on the foot rests.
Q1051 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
An engine seizure is caused by:
  • [A] Changing up a gear too early
  • [B] Not changing gear properly
  • [C] Not enough lubrication in the engine ✔ Correct
  • [D] Damp weather
Explanation: A lack of lubrication causes engine seizure because without oil, the engine's moving parts can't move smoothly against one another. This causes the engine to overheat.
Q1052 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When travelling on a motorcycle, which items are required by law for a passenger? Select all that apply.
  • [A] Helmet ✔ Correct
  • [B] Boots
  • [C] Jacket
  • [D] Leather pants
  • [E] E. Goggles
Explanation: Correct. Legally only a helmet is required, but for added protection; a jacket, long pants, and boots are recommended.
Q1053 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you do if a dog rushes out in front of you?
  • [A] Put on the brakes and swerve to try and avoid hitting it
  • [B] Slow down as much as you can, if there's no other option then hit the animal ✔ Correct
Explanation: Rather than swerving into the path of an oncoming car, you are better off making impact with a small animal such as a dog.
Q1054 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
On a motorbike which brake is the most powerful?
  • [A] Air brake
  • [B] Rear brake
  • [C] Front brake ✔ Correct
Explanation: About 75-90% of the braking performance comes from the front brake.
Q1055 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Counter steering best enables you to do what?
  • [A] Maintain a straight line
  • [B] Swerve around an object ✔ Correct
  • [C] Controls the bike around corners
Explanation: Counter steering is a way of turning quickly on a motorcycle.
Q1056 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
How should the fastest stops be made?
  • [A] Regressive braking
  • [B] Progressive braking ✔ Correct
  • [C] High impact braking
  • [D] Hesitant braking
Explanation: Apply enough braking force to start the transfer of weight to the front wheel, then progressively increase the force on the front brake to make full use of the front tyre gripping the road surface, this is progressive braking. As you slow down release brake pressure to avoid...
Q1057 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Where should you sit to be comfortable when you ride?
  • [A] Your elbows are slightly bent when your hands are on the handlebars and you're sitting far enough back in the seat ✔ Correct
  • [B] Your elbows are quite bent and you are fairly forward in your seat
  • [C] Your arms are straight and your sitting near the back of the seat
Explanation: Far enough back in the seat that your elbows are slightly bent when your hands are on the handlebars.
Q1058 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
A motorbike is often not seen by other road users, why is this? Select all that apply.
  • [A] Drivers of other vehicles fail to look
  • [B] Motorcyclists wear dark colours and are hard to see
  • [C] Compared to a car a motorcycle has a small profile ✔ Correct
  • [D] Saccades - minute eye movements that render us blind for fractions of a second at a time
Explanation: Although drivers usually look, they don't see motorbikes because they are small and may be hidden by road signage or other vehicles. There are scenarios where your bike can be missed if the driver just takes ones glance as we are technically 'blind' between saccades, which are...
Q1059 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
On a slippery surface, what brake(s) should be used?
  • [A] Only the rear
  • [B] Only the front
  • [C] Both, but use the back brake first as gently as possible
  • [D] Both, but use the front brake first and as gently as possible ✔ Correct
Explanation: Gently apply the front brake and then the back brake. Keep the bike upright to avoid the front wheel from washing out. Note that some motorcycle instructors advise you to only use the rear brake in this situation, which contradicts NZTA's information regarding this question.
Q1060 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you do if another driver or rider follows you too closely?
  • [A] Speed up so that they can't pass you
  • [B] Pull to the left to let them past ✔ Correct
  • [C] Hold your line
Explanation: The best and most courteous thing to do is pulling over to the left to let them past.
Q1061 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Holding your knees against the petrol tank will help you do what the most?
  • [A] Build strength to help with control
  • [B] Go faster
  • [C] Better mileage
  • [D] Balance ✔ Correct
Explanation: The main benefit of holding your knees is that it will help you to balance and may make you more aerodynamic.
Q1062 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
If you make a sudden direction or change speed on a slippery surface what can happen?
  • [A] You can lose control if your front wheel skids
  • [B] You can lose control if your back wheel skids
  • [C] You can lose control if either your front or your back wheels skid ✔ Correct
Explanation: Your tyres can leave a skid as quick changes in direction can cause your tyres to overcome the friction of the road.
Q1063 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When riding at night, what is the most important thing to do?
  • [A] Slow down
  • [B] Use your low beam headlights
  • [C] Ensure you are more visible ✔ Correct
  • [D] Follow the vehicles taillights in front of you
Explanation: The most important thing is being visible, but there are other important factors as well. Don't wear tinted eyewear, watch out for pedestrians and cyclists, stop if you are tired, ensure your visor and lights are clean, don't blind others with your lights, ride so you can see at...
Q1064 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Your front wheel locks up when braking, what should you do?
  • [A] To give it more grip put more weight over the wheel
  • [B] To stop the front wheel from 'washing' out from under you put your weight over the rear of the bike
  • [C] Release the front brake ✔ Correct
Explanation: To prevent the front wheel from skidding out from underneath you, release the brake then reapply it.
Q1065 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Is driving a motorcycle more exhausting than driving a car?
  • [A] Yes ✔ Correct
  • [B] No
  • [C] Only on bumpy roads
Explanation: Yes, driving a motorcycle is more tiring than driving a car.
Q1066 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When towing a motorcycle, what is the maximum speed?
  • [A] 20kph
  • [B] 30kph ✔ Correct
  • [C] 40kph
  • [D] 50kph
Explanation: 30kph is the maximum speed when towing a motorbike.
Q1067 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What position in the lane should you be in when passing parked cars?
  • [A] Left
  • [B] Middle
  • [C] Right ✔ Correct
  • [D] Doesn't matter
Explanation: If a car pulls in front of you, you have more room to reach being on the right side. It also removes the chance of a car driver opening a door into your path.
Q1068 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Check all of the motorbike helmet standards that are acceptable in New Zealand:
  • [A] UN/ECE Regulation No. 22 ✔ Correct
  • [B] Australian Standard AS 1698
  • [C] New Zealand Standard NZS 5430
  • [D] British Standard BS 6658
  • [E] E. Japan Industrial Standard T8133
Explanation: The Snell Memorial Foundation, Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard No. 218, along with all of these are valid standards.
Q1069 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Check all of the possible causes of skidding.
  • [A] Over braking on one or both wheels ✔ Correct
  • [B] Heavy acceleration
  • [C] Suddenly changing direction
  • [D] Driving too fast on wet or unsealed roads
Explanation: A (over-braking) is the most common cause, although all are possible causes for skidding.
Q1070 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What is the proper style and fit for a helmet? Check all that apply.
  • [A] It should fit snug ✔ Correct
  • [B] It should always be fastened when riding
  • [C] Ideally it is a bright, visible colour
  • [D] The back and sides should have red reflective material
  • [E] E. None of the internal padding or straps are frayed or loose
Explanation: All answers are correct. Helmets should fit snug and should be fastened so that it is less likely to come off in an accident. Straps or internal padding that are frayed might fail entirely in an accident. The more visible your helmet and you are, the better.
Q1071 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you do in any kind of skid?
  • [A] If it's safe, jump off the bike to increase your chance of surviving impact
  • [B] Stand up on the footrests
  • [C] Stop faster by braking harder
  • [D] Keep both feet on the footrests ✔ Correct
Explanation: Keeping both feet on the foot rests and a lower centre of gravity will help you regain control in a skid. Until traction is regained, you should let off the brake, then reapply the brake.
Q1072 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When may you be permitted to carry a pillion passenger?
  • [A] On a learner licence but only during daylight hours
  • [B] Full Class 1 licence only
  • [C] Only on a full Class 6 licence ✔ Correct
  • [D] On any licence at any time
Explanation: On a full Class 6 licence is when you may carry a pillion passenger.
Q1073 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
In a situation when you are passing parked vehicles, the main dangers include: vehicles pulling out without signalling or vehicles making U-turns when you are passing parked vehicles. True or false?
  • [A] TRUE ✔ Correct
  • [B] FALSE
Explanation: Yes. A motorcyclist has an advantage over drivers when passing parked vehicles because, by staying in the right-hand lane one can avoid problems like drivers getting out of other vehicles, doors opening or people stepping out from between vehicles.
Q1074 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What's the maximum cc of a bike that you are allowed to ride as a restricted licence holder?
  • [A] 50cc
  • [B] 125cc
  • [C] 250cc
  • [D] 400cc
  • [E] E. 660cc (as long as it's LAMS-approved) ✔ Correct
Explanation: There are new rules since October 2012 which introduced LAMS- approved bikes. These have a maximum power-to-weight ratio of 150 kilowatts per tonne (the power is that specified by the manufacturer and the weight is the weight specified by the manufacturer plus 90kgs for the...
Q1075 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you assume if another vehicle can enter your path?
  • [A] Because your light is on it has seen you
  • [B] It could enter your path as it hasn't seen you ✔ Correct
Explanation: Adjust your riding position to compensate as a car may not have seen you and could move into your path.
Q1076 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
How much braking is generated from using the front wheel?
  • [A] 0.5
  • [B] 0.6
  • [C] 0.7
  • [D] More than 70% ✔ Correct
Explanation: 75-90% of the braking performance comes from the front brake.
Q1077 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
If your chain breaks, how will you notice?
  • [A] The engine dies and you lose power
  • [B] Engine over-revs and you lose power ✔ Correct
Explanation: Your engine will lose power and rev higher if your chain breaks. There's also a chance that you will cause a skid if the chain locks the back wheel.
Q1078 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What is the most important thing to remember when carrying a passenger?
  • [A] Because it's heavier, the motorcycle will respond more slowly ✔ Correct
  • [B] You will be less visible because your headlights will be dipped further
  • [C] There's more weight over the rear wheel so you can stop faster
  • [D] The driver should give the passenger(s) more room by moving further forward
Explanation: Correct. If you have the right bike and equipment then the passenger should be able to fit comfortably when you are in the right riding position. Your headlights will be higher with the extra weight on your back, you can risk dazzling drivers. Turning, braking and accelerating...
Q1079 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
A large piece of wood is right in front of you while driving on a suburban street and there is no other option than to driver over it. What should you do to keep control? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Jump off the bike
  • [B] Rise slightly in your seat ✔ Correct
  • [C] Straighten up the bike
  • [D] Loosely hold the grips to absorb any shock
Explanation: You should hold onto the hand grips firmly and straighten up the bike, rise slightly in your seat, and keep a neutral balance.
Q1080 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you do to keep control of your machine if you encounter rough, uneven surfaces? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Keep your head up ✔ Correct
  • [B] Don't resist and try and control the bike's every move, relax.
  • [C] Ride in the left track if there are wheel tracks
  • [D] Right in the right track if there are wheel tracks
  • [E] E. Brake using the rear wheel first
Explanation: Ride in the left wheel track if there is one, and brake using the front brake first. Keep your head up, relax and let the bike move underneath you a little rather than fighting it.
Q1081 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What is the maximum speed you can ride when towing a trailer that is more than half the weight of your motorcycle (including its load)?
  • [A] 40kph ✔ Correct
  • [B] 45kph
  • [C] 65kph
  • [D] 100kph
Explanation: Correct. 40kph is the maximum speed you are allowed to travel on the open road if your trailer is more than half the weight of your bike.
Q1082 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Which of these is best if you're in an emergency situation and you need to control your bike?
  • [A] Look at a target you're trying to miss so that you know where it is and can hopefully avoid it
  • [B] So your hands don't slip and you can see your speed look at your controls
  • [C] Look where you want to go and the bike will typically steer that way ✔ Correct
Explanation: Typically, you will steer automatically in the direction that you are looking to go.
Q1083 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
A motorcyclist is required to wear what by law? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Helmet ✔ Correct
  • [B] Gloves
  • [C] Reflective vest
  • [D] Long trousers
  • [E] E. Boots
Explanation: Correct. Legally you are only required to wear a helmet but others increase your protection in the case of an accident so you are encouraged to wear all of them.
Q1084 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What does this sign mean?
  • [A] A motorcycle may park to the left of this sign ✔ Correct
  • [B] A motorcycle may park 10 metres from this sign
  • [C] A motorcycle can park in the direction of the arrow on the sign
  • [D] This is a lane for motorcycles only
Explanation: Correct. Motorcycles can park to the left of this sign.
Q1085 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Where is the best place on the road to position your motorcycle whilst riding if you're following a vehicle?
  • [A] Behind the right hand wheels of the vehicle in front ✔ Correct
  • [B] As close to the left as you can
  • [C] As close to the right as you can
  • [D] In the middle of the road
Explanation: Correct.
Q1086 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What is the formation called when riding in groups?
  • [A] Double formation
  • [B] Single file
  • [C] Single File
  • [D] Staggered formation ✔ Correct
Explanation: Just like the diagram, you ride in staggered formation.

  • [D] Tilted well down at the front

  • [D] Use your horn to warn drivers ✔ Correct
  • [E] Ride with your foot resting lightly on the foot brake to make the brake light come on

  • [D] In the middle of the lane

  • [A] It will irritate other drivers who may then drive more aggressively towards you

Q1107 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Motorbike - Motorbike-Specific DT Driver Training (Extended)

  • [A] Speed up and move right in your lane
  • [B] Speed up and move left in your lane

  • [E] E. Moving mail
Explanation: Only mail and moving animals are considered goods services; the others aren't.
Q1157 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Who is responsible for ensuring that a load is correctly loaded and secure?
  • [A] Your employer
  • [B] The supplier of the goods
  • [C] The truck/trailer manufacturer
  • [D] The driver ✔ Correct
Explanation: The safety of the load is looked after by the driver.
Q1158 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Where is the front axis on a rigid vehicle that has two axle sets and is steered by the front axle set?
  • [A] The centre point of the foremost axle ✔ Correct
  • [B] The centre point of the passenger's seat
  • [C] The centre point of a trailer
  • [D] The centre point of the back bumper
Explanation: Correct.
Q1159 All Classes Class 3-5 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Where must the road user charges licence for a heavy trailer be displayed? Select all that apply.
  • [A] Inside the windscreen on the passenger's side ✔ Correct
  • [B] On the driver's side, Inside the windscreen
  • [C] On the log book's cover
  • [D] On the right front side of the trailer
  • [E] On the front left side of the trailer
Explanation: The RUC should be displayed on the front left side of the trailer or inside the windscreen on the passenger's side.
Q1160 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
A heavy vehicle has a Gross Vehicle Mass (GVM) surpassing:
  • [A] 3000kg
  • [B] 3500kg ✔ Correct
  • [C] 4000kg
  • [D] 4500kg
Explanation: A heavy vehicle has a gross vehicle mass surpassing 3500kg
Q1161 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What does gross weight mean?
  • [A] The weight of a rigid or combination vehicle with it's load
  • [B] The weight of a rigid or combination vehicle, together with any load it is carrying (including accessories and equipment) ✔ Correct
  • [C] The weight of a rigid or combination vehicle including accessories
  • [D] The weight of a rigid or combination vehicle only, no load or accessories
Explanation: The combined weight of a vehicle and it's load along with it's accessories and equipment is the combined gross weight.
Q1162 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
The maximum rear overhang allowed for a heavy rigid vehicle whose rear-most axle is a non-steering axle is the lesser of:
  • [A] 2m or 50% of the wheelbase
  • [B] 3m or 60% of the wheelbase
  • [C] 4m or 65% of the wheelbase
  • [D] 4m or 70% of the wheelbase ✔ Correct
Explanation: Whichever is lesser, 70% or 4m of the wheelbase.
Q1163 All Classes Class 3-5 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What is the lowest class of licence required to drive a combination vehicle that has a gross combined weight of 14,000kg?
  • [A] Class 3 ✔ Correct
  • [B] Class 4
  • [C] Class 5
  • [D] Class 6
Explanation: Drivers having a class 3 licence are allowed to drive combination vehicles from 12,000-25,000kg.
Q1164 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
A driver must maintain how many logbooks?
  • [A] One ✔ Correct
  • [B] Two- One for your employer and one for the vehicle
  • [C] Three- One for your employer, one for your vehicle, and one for your records
Explanation: Correct. You are only required to keep one logbook.
Q1165 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Including its load, what is the maximum height permitted from the ground for a vehicle?
  • [A] 3.5m plus 25mm for lashings, tarpaulins, straps, chains, or covers
  • [B] 3.75m plus 25mm for lashings, tarpaulins, straps, chains or covers
  • [C] 4.25m plus 25mm for lashings, tarpaulins, straps, chains or covers ✔ Correct
  • [D] 4.75m plus 25mm for lashings, tarpaulins, straps, chains or covers
  • [E] E. 5.5m plus 25mm for lashings, tarpaulins, straps, chains or covers
Explanation: The maximum height is 4.25m and the tensioning devices or straps must not be permanently attached to the vehicle.
Q1166 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Other than for a school bus, what is the maximum speed limit for a heavy motor vehicle?
  • [A] 80kph
  • [B] 85kph
  • [C] 90kph ✔ Correct
  • [D] 95kph
Explanation: On an open road 90kph is the maximum speed a vehicle with a GVM of 3500kg or more must drive.
Q1167 All Classes Class 3-5 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What is the maximum distance a load may extend behind the body of a trailer before an overdimensional flag is required?
  • [A] 1m ✔ Correct
  • [B] 1.25m
  • [C] 1.5m
  • [D] 2.75m
Explanation: An overdimensional flag has to be attached to the end of the load, If a load extends more than 1m behind the vehicle. At night, depending on the load, the flag must be replaced by one or more lights.
Q1168 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
A driver must do a pre-tip safety inspection for what purpose? Check all that apply.
  • [A] It's legally required
  • [B] You can check the load is secured ✔ Correct
  • [C] You can check for safety issues
  • [D] It lowers the risk of being fined or being issued a non-operation order
Explanation: It is a legal requirement to ensure your vehicle is safe and safely loaded. You can do the walk-around inspections yourself if you are a driver or an operator, to ensure that the defects are fixed before you hit the road.
Q1169 All Classes Class 3-5 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
You see this sign, but you are travelling in a heavy motor vehicle pulling two semi-trailers. What is the maximum speed you can travel in this area?
  • [A] 40kph
  • [B] 45kph
  • [C] 55kph
  • [D] 50kph ✔ Correct
Explanation: Here you can travel at the stated limit as you will not go over the limit of 90kph for a heavy motor vehicle.
Q1170 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What is the minimum amount of rest time required after 5.5 hours of consecutive work?
  • [A] 30 minutes ✔ Correct
  • [B] 45 minutes
  • [C] 1 hour
  • [D] 6 hours
Explanation: Correct. You must take a 30-minute break after you have worked 5.5 hours consecutively, unless you have reached 70 hours in a work period or 13 hours in a day, in which case 10 hours or 24 hours' break respectively.
Q1171 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What is the minimum continuous period of rest time that must be taken before starting a new consecutive work day if a driver is subject to work time requirements?
  • [A] 6 hours
  • [B] 10 hours ✔ Correct
  • [C] 12 hours
  • [D] 1 day
Explanation: Before starting a new cumulative work day you must take a break of at least 10 hours.
Q1172 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What is the maximum continuous period of work time permitted before a 30-minute break is required for a driver (other than a taxi driver)?
  • [A] 4.5 hours
  • [B] 5 hours
  • [C] 5.5 hours ✔ Correct
  • [D] 6 hours
Explanation: A driver must take a minimum 30 minute break after working 5.5 consecutive hours.
Q1173 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What is the maximum weight permitted on a single stranded-tyre axle, providing a manufacturer's tyre and axle ratings permit it?
  • [A] 4000kg
  • [B] 6000kg ✔ Correct
  • [C] 7200kg
  • [D] 8200kg
Explanation: 6000kg is the maximum weight permitted on a single standard-tyre axel.
Q1174 All Classes Class 3-5 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What is the maximum forward distance for a heavy motor vehicle with a tow coupling?
  • [A] 8.25m
  • [B] 8.5m ✔ Correct
  • [C] 8.75m
  • [D] 10m
Explanation: The maximum distance with a tow coupling is 8.5m; without one heavy rigid vehicles can have a 9.5m forward distance.
Q1175 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
The maximum overall length for a heavy rigid vehicle including its load, when not towing a trailer, is what?
  • [A] 12m
  • [B] 12.3m
  • [C] 12.6m ✔ Correct
  • [D] 12.9m
Explanation: Not including collapsible mirrors, 12.6m is the maximum length.
Q1176 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What period of time after the last entry must the logbook be retained for every driver in which a logbook is required?
  • [A] 0 months
  • [B] 12 months
  • [C] 24 months
  • [D] 36 months ✔ Correct
Explanation: The correct and latest edition answer is 36 months after the last entry. There is some confusion, until recently this was 12 months. If you have the option of 36 months, choose 36 months and if you have the option of 12 months, choose 12 months, which is the outdated answer. If...
Q1177 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
For securing a load, what additional height is allowed for tarpaulins and lashings, apart from the maximum allowable body or load height of 4.25 metres for a heavy motor vehicle?
  • [A] 25mm ✔ Correct
  • [B] 50mm
  • [C] 75mm
  • [D] 100mm
Explanation: Correct. The tensioning devices or straps must not be forever attached to the vehicle.
Q1178 All Classes Class 3-5 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What is the maximum distance a load may extend out from the side of the body of a trailer before an overdimensional flag is required?
  • [A] 200mm ✔ Correct
  • [B] 325mm
  • [C] 450mm
  • [D] 525mm
Explanation: A warning flag is required if there is more than 200mm jutting out.
Q1179 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
On heavy motor vehicles, what is the combined rated strength of lashings placed over rigid loads against a headboard?
  • [A] Twice the weight of the load
  • [B] The weight of the load ✔ Correct
  • [C] Half the weight of the load
Explanation: The lashings must be able to survive the full load weight.
Q1180 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What is the maximum weight permitted on a twin-tyre axle, providing the manufacturer's tyre and axle ratings are not exceeded?
  • [A] 6200kg
  • [B] 7200kg
  • [C] 8200kg ✔ Correct
  • [D] 9200kg
Explanation: A twin-tyre axle has a wheel track of 1.3 metres or more and has four or more tyres. It shouldn't carry any more than 8200kg.
Q1181 All Classes Class 3-5 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What is the maximum overall length for any heavy motor vehicle towing two trailers and including their load?
  • [A] 16m
  • [B] 15m
  • [C] 17m
  • [D] 21m
  • [E] 20m ✔ Correct
Explanation: The maximum total length for any heavy motor vehicle towing two trailers is 20m. This length applies to all types (A-train, B-train, pole trailer or simple trailer).
Q1182 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What is the maximum forward distance for a heavy rigid vehicle without a tow coupling?
  • [A] 8.5m
  • [B] 9m
  • [C] 9.5m ✔ Correct
  • [D] 10m
Explanation: With a tow coupling it is 8.5m, and without a tow coupling it is 9.5m.
Q1183 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
The rear red light of a heavy goods service vehicle must be visible from what distance? (Hint: not an over-dimension vehicle)
  • [A] 50m
  • [B] 100m ✔ Correct
  • [C] 150m
  • [D] 200m
Explanation: A rear-facing red light that is visible at least 100m away and is on the side of the vehicle closest to the centre line is required for heavy motor vehicles and vehicles fitted with a flat deck or tray for carrying goods that are parked on the street at night. The lights must be...
Q1184 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What is the maximum work time permitted in a cumulative work period if a driver is subject to work time requirements?
  • [A] 60 hours
  • [B] 70 hours ✔ Correct
  • [C] 80 hours
  • [D] 90 hours
Explanation: In one work period, the maximum cumulative time in any work period is 70 hours before you must take a 24 hr break.
Q1185 All Classes Class 3-5 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What class of licence is required to drive a combination vehicle that has a gross combined weight of 25,500kg?
  • [A] Class 3
  • [B] Class 4
  • [C] Class 5 ✔ Correct
  • [D] Class 6
Explanation: Drivers with a class 5 licence are allowed to drive combination vehicles of more than 25,000kg.
Q1186 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

  • [A] 25mm each side ✔ Correct
  • [B] 50mm each side
  • [C] 75mm each side
  • [D] 100mm each side
Explanation: Correct. Fasteners are permitted an additional 25mm per side and the tensioning devices or straps must not be permanently or rigidly fixed to the vehicle.
Q1187 All Classes Class 3-5 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Between which points is the forward distance of a semi-trailer measured?
  • [A] The distance between the mid-point of the rear and front axis of the semi-trailer to the front of the vehicle or load
  • [B] The distance inbetween the centre of the kingpin and the rear axis of the semi-trailer ✔ Correct
  • [C] The distance between the front of the vehicle or its load and the rear axis of the semi-trailer to
  • [D] The distance from the front of the trailer to the rear axis (excluding any drawbars and/or the front axle set)
Explanation: The forward distance is measured between the rear axis and the centre of the kingpin.
Q1188 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
You can get an overweight permit from where?
  • [A] Your local NZTA office ✔ Correct
  • [B] The police station
  • [C] The fire station
  • [D] Your employer
Explanation: Correct. The driver must obtain an overweight permit which must be carried in the vehicle before an overweight vehicle or load can be used on the road.
Q1189 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What is the maximum period of work time allowed in any cumulative work day if a driver is subject to work time requirements?
  • [A] 11 hours
  • [B] 12 hours
  • [C] 13 hours ✔ Correct
  • [D] 14 hours
Explanation: In any day, the maximum cumulative time in one day is 13 hrs. A 10-hour rest period is required after each 13 hour period.
Q1190 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What is the most important thing to look for when you are checking your load?
  • [A] Load security ✔ Correct
  • [B] Load height
  • [C] Load width
  • [D] Load weight
Explanation: Correct. It is important to check all of these, and if they are not within the prescribed limits you may be breaking the law. An unsecured load could fall on another vehicle causing serious or life threatening injuries.
Q1191 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Including it's load, what is the maximum vehicle width permitted? (other than an agriculture vehicle)
  • [A] 2m
  • [B] 2.5m ✔ Correct
  • [C] 3m
  • [D] 3.5m
  • [E] E. 4m
Explanation: 1.25m each side of a longitudinal centre line with a maximum of 2.5m.
Q1192 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

  • [C] Check your load ✔ Correct
  • [D] You aren't required to do anything, nothing changes
Explanation: If you drive on an uneven surface loads may become loose or shift.
Q1193 All Classes Class 3-5 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Where on a heavy trailer should a warrant or certificate of fitness be displayed? Check all that apply.
  • [A] At the rear of the trailer near the registration plate ✔ Correct
  • [B] Near the back of the trailer on the right-hand side.
  • [C] At the trailer's front

Q1194 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

  • [A] Registration number ✔ Correct

  • [C] Fuel mileage
  • [D] Start and finish distance recorder readings (if subject to road user charges)

Explanation: In the logbook, you must keep the start and finish distance recorder readings and you must keep the registration number.
Q1195 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What must the combined strength of the tie downs be for a load of 10 tones carried on a rigid truck with no headboard and secured by two tie downs?
  • [A] 5 tonnes
  • [B] 10 tonnes
  • [C] 15 tonnes
  • [D] 20 tonnes ✔ Correct
Explanation: The lashings need to be able to survive the load weight.
Q1196 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

  • [C] The weight of the vehicle plus the load
  • [D] The weight of the vehicle minus the load weight
Explanation: Not including any load, the tare weight is the weight of the vehicle itself.
Q1197 All Classes Class 3-5 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What is the maximum height of a heavy motor vehicle from the ground (not including straps, lashings, coverings, etc)?
  • [A] 3.75m
  • [B] 4.25m ✔ Correct
  • [C] 4.5m
  • [D] 5.0m
Explanation: 4.25 metres above ground is the maximum height. You are allowed an additional 25 millimetres for tarpaulins, lashings, straps, chains, covers and related connectors and tensioning devices that aren't permanently or rigidly fixed to the vehicle.
Q1198 All Classes Class 3-5 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
From what distance must the rear red light of a heavy goods service vehicle be visible? (note: not an over-dimension load)
  • [A] 75m
  • [B] 100m ✔ Correct
  • [C] 125m
  • [D] 175m
Explanation: Heavy motor vehicles that are parked on the street at night are required to display a red light that is visible at least 100m away and is on the side of the vehicle closest to the centre line. For over-dimension vehicle the lights must be visible from at least 200m during the...
Q1199 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What is the minimum continuous rest time to be taken before a new cumulative work period begins if a driver is subject to work time requirements?
  • [A] 10 hours
  • [B] 15 hours
  • [C] 24 hours ✔ Correct
  • [D] 36 hours
Explanation: You must take a minimum 24-hour rest period after a consecutive work period of 70 hours.
Q1200 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
It is the responsibility of who to ensure a permit is carried for over dimensional and overweight loads?
  • [A] Your employer
  • [B] The goods supplier
  • [C] The trailer manufacturer
  • [D] The driver ✔ Correct
Explanation: This is the responsibility of the driver.
Q1201 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Loose bulk loads that are uncovered possibly could fall from the vehicle if they are higher than:
  • [A] 200mm below the height of the vehicle body
  • [B] 100mm below the side of the vehicle body ✔ Correct
  • [C] The same height as the vehicle
  • [D] 100mm higher than the vehicle's doors
Explanation: 100mm below the height of the vehicle body is the maximum that uncovered loose bulk loads should be loaded.
Q1202 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What is the maximum you can be fined if you fail to produce an approved logbook when asked by an enforcement office?
  • [A] $2,000 ✔ Correct
  • [B] $5,000
  • [C] $10,000
  • [D] $25,000
Explanation: Correct. 35 demerit points will also be applied to your licence.
Q1203 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
You should check your load at what time? Check all that apply.
  • [A] After driving in poor weather conditions
  • [B] After driving over uneven ground ✔ Correct
  • [C] Every 300km
  • [D] After each rest stop
Explanation: After each rest stop or if you have driven over an uneven road is when you should check your load.
Q1204 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
You are traveling in a heavy motor vehicle and you see this sign. In this area what is the maximum speed you can travel?
  • [A] 50kph
  • [B] 60kph
  • [C] 65kph
  • [D] 70kph ✔ Correct
Explanation: As a heavy motor vehicle, you will not exceed the absolute speed limit of 90kph, so you can drive at the stated limit here.
Q1205 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
A loading certificate for a heavy motor vehicle, must include what weight limits?
  • [A] Tare weight in kg
  • [B] Gross laden weight in kg
  • [C] Gross combination weight in kg (if the vehicle has a towing connection)
  • [D] All of the above ✔ Correct
Explanation: All of the above, answer D.
Q1206 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What must the combined strength of the tie downs be equal to or stronger than for a load of 15 tonnes carried on a rigid truck with a headboard secured by two tie downs?
  • [A] 5 tonnes
  • [B] 10 tonnes
  • [C] 15 tonnes ✔ Correct
  • [D] 20 tonnes
Explanation: The lashings need to be able to survive the load weight.
Q1207 All Classes Class 3-5 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What is the maximum speed limit for a heavy motor vehicle towing a semi-trailer or semi-trailers?
  • [A] 75kph
  • [B] 80kph
  • [C] 90kph ✔ Correct
  • [D] 100kph
Explanation: When towing one or more semi trailers a vehicle must not exceed 90kph on the open road.
Q1208 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
A vehicle and it's load on either side of the longitudinal centre line is permitted what maximum width?
  • [A] 1.25m ✔ Correct
  • [B] 1.5m
  • [C] 2m
  • [D] 2.5m
Explanation: Correct. On either side of the centre line the maximum width is 1.25m, which is an overall maximum width of 2.5m.
Q1209 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
To carry dangerous goods how often do you have to renew your endorsement?
  • [A] 1 year
  • [B] 2 years
  • [C] 3 years
  • [D] 5 years ✔ Correct
Explanation: To carry dangerous goods which includes flammable liquids, explosives, toxic substances, corrosive substances and oxidising agents you must renew your endorsement every 5 years.
Q1210 All Classes Class 3-5 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What is the forward distance of a full trailer (other than a pole trailer), the front axle of which is steered by a towbar?
  • [A] The distance between the mid-point of the rear and front axis of the trailer to the front of the vehicle or load
  • [B] The distance inbetween front of the vehicle or its loadand the front axis of the trailer
  • [C] The distance between to the front of the vehicle or its load and the rear axis of the trailer
  • [D] The distance from the front of the trailer to the rear axis (excluding any drawbars and/or the front axle set) ✔ Correct
Explanation: From the rear axis to the front of the trailer (the forward distance) the maximum distance is 8.5m.
Q1211 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Is a driver required to do a pre-trip safety inspection?
  • [A] Yes. It's a legal requirement
  • [B] Yes. It's for safety reasons ✔ Correct
  • [C] No. Only if weight of the load changed
Explanation: You may have to complete some items that are a legal requirement during a pre-trip check, for example affixing dangerous goods signs, but it is not a legal requirement.
Q1212 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Load restraint systems should be able to withstand how much weight? (sideways)
  • [A] Twice the weight of the load
  • [B] The weight of the load
  • [C] Half the weight of the load ✔ Correct
Explanation: At least half the weight of the load to keep it secure is what the load restraint system must be able to handle.
Q1213 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
On a Class 2 licence, what types of vehicles can you drive? Check all that apply.
  • [A] A rigid vehicle (including any tractor) with a GLW of more than 6000kg but less than 18,000kg ✔ Correct
  • [B] A combination vehicle (that is not a tractor/trailer combination) with a GCW of not more than 12,000kg
  • [C] A combination vehicle (that is not a tractor) consisting of a rigid vehicle with a GLW of 18,000kg or less towing a light trailer (GLW of 3500kg or less)
  • [D] A rigid vehicle with a GLW of more than 18,000kg that has no more than two axles
  • [E] E. A tractor with a GLW of more than 6000kg but not more than 18,000kg, if driven at a speed over 30km/h
Explanation: Incorrect, all of the above in addition to a special-type of vehicle * runs on wheels and has a GLW of more than 18,000kg but does not exceed over 30km/h ( Class D licence required), a tractor if driven at a speed over 30km/h and has a GLW of more than 6000kg
Q1214 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Anchor points to which lashings are fastened, must have a strength of at least:
  • [A] Half the strength of the lashings
  • [B] At least the rated strength of the lashings ✔ Correct
  • [C] Twice the strength as the lashings
Explanation: The anchor points must have at minimum, the same strength as the lashings.
Q1215 All Classes Class 3-5 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
For a heavy full trailer, the maximum rear overhang including its load is the lesser of:
  • [A] 4m or 50% of the wheelbase ✔ Correct
  • [B] 4m or 65% of the wheelbase
  • [C] 6m or 50% of the wheelbase
  • [D] 5m or 65% of the wheelbase
Explanation: It is 4m or 50% of the wheelbase for a heavy full trailer.
Q1216 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What kind of axle set is it when a vehicle has two load-sharing axles spaced 1.5 metres apart?
  • [A] Tri-axle
  • [B] Tandem axle ✔ Correct
  • [C] Twin-steer axle
  • [D] Double-axle
Explanation: A tandem axle indicates two axles where the middles are spaced no less than 1 metre and no more than 2 metres apart.
Q1217 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What is the latest time that you must take a break if you are a driver (other than a taxi driver) and your work starts at 7am?
  • [A] 11:30am
  • [B] 12:00pm
  • [C] 12:30pm ✔ Correct
  • [D] 01:00pm
Explanation: You will need to take your break before 12:30pm because you can only work 5.5 hours before having to take a break.
Q1218 All Classes Class 3-5 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What is the maximum width permitted for a heavy trailer (other than an agricultural trailer) from its longitudinal centre line?
  • [A] 1.1m
  • [B] 1.25m ✔ Correct
  • [C] 1.6m
  • [D] 1.75m
Explanation: For a heavy rigid vehicle the same applies - 1.25m.
Q1219 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
You must deliver a copy of each completed log book record to your employer within what period of time if you are employed as a driver?
  • [A] 1 day
  • [B] 1 week
  • [C] 2 weeks ✔ Correct
  • [D] 1 month
Explanation: The 'record' copy must be delivered within 14 days to your employer.
Q1220 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
From the front edge of the driver's seat (in its rearmost position), what is the maximum distance a vehicle or its load may extend forward?
  • [A] 2m
  • [B] 3m ✔ Correct
  • [C] 4m
  • [D] 5m
Explanation: Three metres is the maximum distance.
Q1221 All Classes Class 2 Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
If you are driving a rigid vehicle that has a gross combined weight of 12,000kg, what is the lowest class of licence required?
  • [A] Class 2 ✔ Correct
  • [B] Class 3
  • [C] Class 4
  • [D] Class 5
